articleTitle: A New Method to Detect DMR Faults During Balanced Condition for a VSC Bipole Onshore-Offshore HVDC Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The bipole High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) systems can transmit high power rating when compared with monopole HVDC link. The flexibility and reliability that is provided by the bipole configuration make it an attractive solution for power transmission from offshore wind farms to onshore grid. These bipole HVDCs have dedicated metallic return (DMR) as a return path and ground references. The detection of fault in the DMR cable of a bipole HVDC is a challenging task. Traditional over-current and differential protection fail to detect the faults in the network. In this paper, the moving window-based Pearson correlation coefficient (MWPCC), variational mode decomposition (VMD) and bagging ensemble classifier (BEC) based two fault detection algorithms are proposed. The first two advanced signal processing methods are utilized to extract data for the classifier. The effectiveness of the proposed detection technique is demonstrated by applying different fault scenarios. The time domain simulations are performed using a full-scale industrial model, and the fault detection algorithms have achieved very high accuracy to detect the fault.

articleTitle: DSOGI Based Power Quality Control with Grid Connected SECS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The paper presents a grid-connected solar energy conversion system (SECS) designed to deliver power both to the grid and a nonlinear load. It utilizes a Dual Second Order Generalized Integrator (DSOGI) controller for a D-STATCOM-type Voltage Source Converter (VSC). In comparison with traditional algorithms, this controller ensures balanced grid currents, corrects the power factor to unity, and mitigates harmonics even under challenging conditions such as unbalanced nonlinear loads, variations in solar irradiation, and grid voltage disturbances. The Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, based on the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method, is implemented to optimize power extraction from the photovoltaic array. The system's performance and robustness are tested by giving practice disturbance that includes load imbalances and sudden changes in solar irradiation. The real-time performance of the system is also evaluated using the Opal-RT OP4510 simulator. The study fully complies with harmonic control standards IEEE std. 519.

articleTitle: Voltage Regulation of DC-DC Boost Converter Using PI Controller in Cascade Control Structure
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this paper, a simple PI controller for voltage regulation of the DC-DC boost converter having non-minimum phase characteristic is presented. The structure of the proposed controller is designed in a cascade mode. To apply the controller, the transfer function of the DC-DC boost converter is modelled using state averaging technique. The control parameters of the suggested PI controllers are -obtained using an optimization technique-Differential Evolution by minimizing a suitable performance measure. The suggested control technique is investigated in MATLAB/Simulink for set-point tracking and disturbance rejection for voltage regulation under changes in input voltage and load-resistance. Finally, robustness of the proposed controller is also analyzed by introducing parametric perturbations in boost converter circuit model. The hardware validation of the proposed controller is being carried out in the laboratory and it will be reflected in the modified version of this paper.

articleTitle: Leader-Follower Consensus Control of Multi-Agent Systems With Disturbance by Distributed Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper addresses the leader-follower consensus control of multi-agent systems (MASs) in the presence of external disturbance, utilizing a distributed sliding mode control (DSMC) approach. We first formulate the consensus problem, where a designated leader influences the behavior of multiple follower agents. The proposed DSMC strategy is designed to enhance robustness against disturbances and uncertainties inherent in the system. By leveraging the sliding mode control theory, we ensure that the agents maintain desired trajectories while effectively rejecting external perturbations. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the stability and convergence of the consensus protocol, supported by simulation results showcasing the efficacy of the DSMC method in practical scenarios. This work contributes to the field of multi-agent systems by providing a reliable control framework capable of achieving consensus under challenging conditions, making it applicable in various domains, including robotics and autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Fault Ride Through Capability of DFIG based Wind Energy Conversion System using Improved Intersecting Type Fault Current Limiter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The most common machine for wind power applications is the doubly fed induction generator (DFIG), which can operate at varied speeds and control DC link voltage by using power electronics converters. Even though DFIG-based generators are the most common, they are especially prone to grid voltage fluctuations. The present system increases the stability due to fault ride through (FRT), as FRT is very important for DFIG based wind energy conversion systems (WECS). In a DFIG-based model, an intersecting type fault current limiter (ITFCL) is employed to improve the FRT's capabilities, such as DC link voltage, stator current and stator voltage. Electromagnetic torque is also improved. ITFCL also enhances the scheme's short stability, energy performance, and efficiency by reducing error flow suddenly. The literature review presents a superconductivity-based enhanced current limiter solution. The paper's topic is “Intersecting type fault current limiters.” This paper creates a typical DFIG model with ITFCL using Simulink/SimPowerSystem, and LG and LLL-G faults are analyzed both with and without ITFCL.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Droop and VSG Controlled Grid Forming Inverters Integrated with D-STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: With the rise of Distributed Energy Resources (DER), the grid-forming inverter (GFMI) has become a key focus area in modern power systems. This paper presents a comparative performance analysis of two GFMIs controlled_by similar and different controls (Droop and Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) control) integrated with D-STATCOM based on settling time, stability with the effect of PI gains of D-STATCOM's controller. This study finds that Droop controlled GFMIs settle faster than Droop-VSG and VSG controlled GFMIs. However, Droop-VSG provides the least peak overshoots to D-STATCOM. The increased PI gain values of a controller of D-STATCOM provide faster stability of the system. The analysis is conducted using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Influence of TiO2 and SiO2 Nanoparticles on the Dielectric Properties and Breakdown Voltage of Blended Oil
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This study examines the effect of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles on the dielectric properties of a blended oil composed of 80% mineral oil and 20% synthetic ester. By incorporating Tio<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, the dielectric constant, dielectric loss constant, Conductivity, and Polarization current increase. articleTitle: Marine Microgrid Frequency Regulation: Utilizing Diverse Power Generation and Enhanced Nonlinear Control Strategies with Energy Storage Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper describes an independent marine microgrid using RESs for improving load stability and frequency. The Tidal Power Generators, Wind Turbine Generators, Photovoltaic, and Archimedes Wave Energy Conversion are used in the sources of energy while controlled generation units such as MHTG and Biodiesel Engine Generators are used by the microgrid. To counter both generation and load imbalances, the research utilizes energy storage systems, which further enhance microgrid flexibility. These include fuel cells, ultracapacitors, flywheel energy storage systems, and battery energy storage systems. A fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative (FOPID) controller is used to cope with load frequency control as well as grid stability with efficiency in different load fluctuation scenarios. The paper discusses the optimization of FOPID controller parameters using Heap-Based Optimization (HBO), Coati Optimization, Artificial Rabbit Optimization, and the Chimpanzee Optimization Algorithm. The proposed HBO algorithm resulted in better simulation results compared to the other algorithms. This approach makes possible the future implementation of microgrids characterized by enhanced operational efficiency, reliability, stability, and extensive use of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Integrating Solar Power with Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Technology for Improved Grid Reliability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper addresses the persistent challenge of ‘range anxiety’ in electric vehicle (EV) adoption by integrating Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) charging with solar panels on the source vehicle. The V2G system allows surplus energy, not required for Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) charging, to be fed back into the grid, thereby enhancing grid stability. It starts by discussing the existing challenges of range anxiety and the limitations of traditional EV charging infrastructure. The paper then elaborates on the design and implementation of solar panels on the source vehicle, emphasizing their efficiency in energy generation. To validate the proposed approach, the perform simulations using MATLAB/Simulink and hardware tests on the Opal-RT simulator, providing a thorough evaluation of our V2G charging system's efficacy. Our contribution lies in advancing innovative solutions for the EV industry, particularly in enhancing grid stability through V2G solutions. This integrated approach underscores the potential of V2G charging, combined with solar panels, in fostering a sustainable and anxiety-free future for EV users. Key objectives include detailing V2G charging mechanisms, outlining solar integration strategies, conducting rigorous simulations and hardware tests, and providing actionable insights for the continued advancement of electric vehicle technology.

articleTitle: The Reliability Enhancement of Power System Using Distribution STATCOM Units with Enhanced Capacitive Reactive Power Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The share of electricity generation through renewable energy resources has exponentially increased from 10% to 30% from 2010 to 2022, and it is expected to grow to 42 % by 2028. Alternatively, distribution power losses and power quality are challenging in terms of grid efficacy, power quality, cost, etc. It has been established that flexible AC transmission systems are very helpful in the power system network for strengthening stability and efficacy. This paper presents the enhancement of the power system using the distribution STATCOM (static synchronous compensator) with improved capacitive reactive power operation. In addition, the constrains related to the influencing of capacitive reactive power limits are detailed. In this paper, the authors specify specific information of commercially accessible converter systems to support computations and estimate its control over the final solution. Reflecting the above, the planned approach is employed on a real 10 MW 6.6 kV medium voltage power converter model connected in 33 kV line and outcomes are quantified and assessed from a reactive power capacity, effectiveness and cost evaluation.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation Characteristics of Hybrid Microgrid Supported by Bio-Renewable Cogeneration with Modified Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper explores the coordinated operation of an airport microgrid with a ship-based microgrid incorporating several sources of renewable energy along with various types of energy storage systems (ESS) and adjustable load elements. A FOPID controller is used in the paper for the frequency regulation, load demand, area control error, and power generation in different areas of load. The FOPID controller gains were optimized using the proposed Mountain Gazelle Optimisation (MGO) algorithm, which was chosen for its accuracy and fast convergence. Along with MGO, the performance of the controller is tested against a number of algorithms, such as the Artificial Electric Field Algorithm (AEFA), Swarm Optimization Algorithm (SO), and Chimp Optimization Algorithm (Choa). Performance indicators the system's resilience and efficiency were assessed using various metrics, including Integrated Square Error (ISE), Integrated Absolute Time Error (IATE), Integrated Absolute Error (IAE), and Integrated Squared Time Error (ISTE). Simulation results confirm the stability and reliability of the systems in the presence of dynamic load demand variation, thus proving its capability as an efficient microgrid. This comparative study shows that MGO is more effective than any other algorithm in managing uncertainties in renewable energy sources and maximizing performance in a system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Panel Efficiency: An IoT-Integrated Machine Learning Approach for Dust Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: India faces significant energy challenges due to rising demand and environmental concerns from fossil fuel use. Solar energy, abundant in India, offers a sustainable solution, but its efficiency is compromised by dust accumulation, especially in arid regions. This research develops an image-based machine learning model using EfficientNet to detect dust on solar panels, integrated with an IoT system featuring ESP32-CAM and Flask for automated cleaning. Utilizing a dataset of 2,563 labeled images, the EfficientNet model outperformed ResNet50 in accuracy and efficiency. The IoT system effectively triggered automated cleaning or sent alerts for manual intervention, optimizing solar panel performance. This integration of machine learning and IoT demonstrates significant potential for enhancing solar energy efficiency, reducing maintenance costs, and supporting renewable energy adoption.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Analysis of Passive Balancing for Parallel Lithium-Ion Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The cell balancing in electric vehicles delivers the maximum energy into or out of the cell during charging or discharging. The proposed system simulates the passive cell balancing of a three-cell lithium-ion battery system by developing a Simulink model using the soc parameter. The initial State of Charge of the cells is 22%, 25%, and 27%. Voltage and current sensors monitor the state of each cell while a calibrated current source controls the rate of balancing depending on the SOC difference. To remove generated heat, convection heat transfer is employed to reduce thermal accumulation in resistors and nearby cells. SOC convergence is achieved where the balancing current decreases as the SOC levels approach an optimal level. This method is thus well suited for applications in which cost and low power consumption are desirable, and consistent performance.

articleTitle: Sensorless Speed Control of Induction Motors using DWT-Integrated Ultra Local Model based MRAS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: An accurate speed estimate is essential for attaining reliable and efficient sensorless control of induction motors, especially in the presence of parameter mismatches and noisy operational environments. This research examines the efficacy of a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT)-augmented Ultra Local Model-based Model Reference Adaptive System (MRAS-ULM) for estimating rotor speed. A comparative examination of dynamic response and frequency spectrum is performed between the traditional MRAS-ULM and the proposed DWT-enhanced MRAS-ULM. Results indicate that the incorporation of DWT markedly enhances noise reduction and signal integrity. At rated speeds, the proposed technique diminishes the higher magnitude of harmonic content, while at low speeds, it guarantees reliable tracking by alleviating noise effects. Frequency spectrum analysis verifies significant attenuation of higher magnitude components and diminished harmonic content, underscoring the efficacy of the suggested technique. These findings confirm that the DWT-enhanced MRAS-ULM is suitable for accurate and dependable speed estimates in induction motor control applications.

articleTitle: Modelling and Design of Wide Voltage Range Buck-Boost Converter for Fuel Cell Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) require efficient power management to maintain optimal battery performance despite fluctuating fuel cell outputs. In this paper, a novel DC-DC converter capable of operating in both buck and boost modes is proposed to address these challenges. Positioned between the battery and fuel cell, the converter ensures a stable voltage supply, enhancing power flow capability. The proposed topology can provide high voltage gain, enabling effective voltage regulation despite a wide range of input variations in the fuel cell, which is crucial for consistent battery charging. Its design employs fewer components than traditional converters, reducing complexity, cost, and potential points of failure. The incorporation of a high-frequency transformer ensures electrical isolation between the input (fuel cell) and output (battery), improving safety by protecting the battery and other vehicle components from potential electrical faults or fluctuations in the FC output. The compact design and efficient operation of the presented converter results in high power density, contributing to overall vehicle design optimization and performance. The design of the presented converter is verified in the MATLAB Simulink, and the corresponding results are shown.

articleTitle: Intelligent Driving Assistance and Alert System for Learners
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: A driving assistance system powered by the ESP32 microcontroller is designed in this paper, to enhance the skills of learner drivers while actively reducing engine strain. The device offers real-time monitoring and display of clutch, brake, and accelerator usage, providing immediate and actionable feedback. It issues critical warnings when the driver engages in potentially risky behaviors, such as simultaneously applying the clutch and accelerator at high speeds or pressing both the accelerator and brake. By guiding learners away from these common mistakes, the system boosts driving safety and protects the engine from unnecessary strain, ensuring smoother and more reliable vehicle performance. With its precise sensor integration and user-friendly display, this device is a valuable tool for mastering proper driving techniques, ultimately contributing to a safer and more efficient driving experience.

articleTitle: Modeling and Performance Analysis of Novel Asymmetric 11-Level Solar Inverter Using PDPWM Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel asymmetric 11-level solar multilevel inverter (MLI), modeled using the Phase Disposition Pulse Width Modulation (PDPWM) technique for home application. Three solar photovoltaic (PV) panels with a 1: 1:3 ratio, optimized for maximum efficiency in power conversion within residential environments, are being used to harness power in the proposed inverter. One salient feature of the proposed design is the reduced form of switch topology with only 7 switches to obtain the desired output of 11 levels, which has minimized both complexity and switching losses. Therefore, it has been developed, based on a totally new coherent mathematical model to simulate the performance of the inverter under practical operating conditions by improving efficiency, reducing total harmonic distortion (THD), and enhancing quality of the output voltage. In summary, this work shows many improvements of efficiency and performance with solar-based systems and offers a strong cost-effective solution for residential renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Power Management for Renewable Energy Integrated Electric Vehicle Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The growing adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) introduces significant challenges, particularly in meeting the rising electricity demand. This situation underscores the importance of incorporating sustainable energy sources at Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS). The main power source for modern charging is a grid, an Energy Storage System (ESS) of the right size and sustainable sources like Photo Voltaic (PV). One significant advancement in this configuration is the real-time cooperation between multiple energy sources, such as the grid, ESS, and PV systems. This integration enables the charging station to operate independently for extended periods, utilizing solar Energy to meet EV charging requirements. The ESS plays a crucial role by storing energy produced by the photovoltaic system, which is used when grid and solar are unavailable. The Energy Management System (EMS) optimizes the use of renewable energy by prioritizing PV power for charging. Doing so reduces reliance on grid electricity, ultimately lowering operational costs and environmental impact. The effectiveness of the EMS has been assessed through simulations of the EVCS under various solar irradiance conditions, evaluating its ability to maximize renewable energy usage and maintain reliable charging services. Integrating PV power, ESS, and EV charging stations grid connectivity with an efficient EMS offers a sustainable solution to the challenges posed by increasing EV adoption, promoting greater energy efficiency and environmental sustainability.

Author Keywords: Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT),Proportional Integral Deferential (PID)

articleTitle: Lyapunov-Based Feedback Control Stabilization of Uncertain Wheeled Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents a disturbance control strategy for wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) that employs nonsmooth integral manifold feedback stabilization for a higher-order uncertain chain of integrators. We address the global adaptive experimental tracking problem for uncertain nonstrict feedback nonlinear systems with unknown control coefficients. The non-restrictive feedback condition, and to ensure controllability in tracking, an innovative dual dynamic gain scaling mechanism is introduced. This nonsmooth controller-based Lyapunov analysis is derived for the closed-loop system, assuring stability and preserving invariance against matched Lipschitz uncertainty. Experimental results on WMRs corroborate the efficacy of this control strategy.

articleTitle: Centralized-Decentralized Control Scheme for Power Sharing in Multiple PV-Battery System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: To reducing the dependency on fossil fuels, there has been a significant shift towards use of renewable energy sources (RESs), particularly solar photovoltaic (PV), leading to the development of microgrids (MGs) within existing distribution systems. The intermittency of PV energy generation is managed with battery storage solutions. Effective control in these MG systems is critical for handling fluctuating power production, ensure optimal balanced power sharing among multiple parallel PV systems, accommodating to time-varying load demands, and prioritizing essential loads during energy shortages. This work gives a centralized-decentralized secondary controller (CDSC) aimed at synchronizing the operations of multiple PV-battery (PVB) units in the MG. Here, the centralized secondary controller (CSC) analyzes settings based on data from the local controller (LC), while the decentralized secondary controller (DSC) uses information from both the CSC and LC measurements to establish reference points for the LC. The CDSC design also takes into account for the actual power output from the PV array and incorporates constraints on the battery's charging/discharging currents, thereby extending the batteries lifespan. This control scheme is rigorously tested across various operational scenarios on a European distribution network using the PSCAD/EMTDC platform. The results suggests it is successful in achieving local distributed generation (DG) controllability as well as global optimality over the distribution network.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective SPV Integration for Improved Grid Reliability and Sustainable Energy Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The paper has presented research to prove integration of SPV at optimal locations, boost voltage profile, reduce loss of system avoiding congestion in transmission system. The study also highlights that use of SPV (solar photovoltaic) has improved grid stability with low cost achieving great economic benefits. The proposed research has been tested on IEEE57 Bus system with integration of SPV at two optimal locations. The strategic location has been investigated with help of Line Stability Index (Lmn). The combination of two locations has been considered as one study case with constant size of SPV plant. The ETAP software (19.1) has been used to run load flow on different study cases. Integration of SPV at Multiple Location enhances system performance, making it a viable strategy for modern power systems. The strategic installation of SPV systems at optimal locations improves grid efficiency, reduces energy costs, and presents a sustainable solution for meeting future energy demands.

articleTitle: Comparison and analysis of Single-Phase and Three-Phase Static Wireless Charging for E-Auto Rickshaws
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) charging by static wireless charging is growing in popularity worldwide.Wireless charging technology for electric rickshaws (e-rickshaws) has emerged as a promising solution to overcome the limitations of conventional wired charging systems, such as physical wear, safety concerns, and charging downtime. This study explores and compares single-phase and three-phase wireless charging systems for e-rickshaws, focusing on their operational principles, efficiency, and suitability for urban transportation. The single-phase wireless charging system, characterized by its simpler design and cost-effectiveness, is ideal for light-duty e-rickshaws operating in low-power scenarios. However, it often suffers from lower power transfer efficiency and slower charging rates. On the other hand, the three-phase wireless charging system offers higher power transfer efficiency, faster charging times, and better scalability for heavy-duty applications, though it comes with increased complexity and cost.By analyzing the design challenges, electro-magnetic interference issues, and overall performance of both systems, this study highlights the trade-offs between efficiency and cost-effectiveness. Furthermore, the feasibility of integrating wireless charging systems with renewable energy sources and their potential role in developing sustainable, smart cities is discussed. The findings serve as a foundation for selecting and optimizing wireless charging technologies tailored to the specific needs of e-rickshaws in different settings.It also presents the results of Single phase and three-phase sources based SWCS with a 40% coupling coefficient at 85KHz switching frequency. The overall comparison analysis was done by using LTSpice software.

articleTitle: Thermal Optimization of Microprocessor Chip Used in Power Electronics Devices with Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This research aims to bridge the existing knowledge gap in microprocessor chip binning based on performance by applying the machine learning (ML) techniques. The concept of performance binning is examined, where units undergo thorough testing to categorize them according to factors such as Vmin and frequency. Performance binning ensures that units with similar performance traits are grouped together, streamlining quality assurance and optimizing production processes. By integrating machine learning into the binning process of microprocessor chip units, potential benefits include reduced burn-in, shorter testing times, and minimized thermal stresses on the chips which help for thermal optimization of the chip. Notably, employing linear regression reveals a maximum percentage variation of 2.45% for high frequency. These advancements not only optimize production but also have a significant impact on chip performance. Specifically, minimizing thermal stresses and excess voltage enhances chip reliability, energy efficiency, and operational longevity. The proposed model, utilizing linear regression for binning, demonstrates resilience by reducing excess voltage and optimizing the production process.

articleTitle: Adaptive Protection Based Fault Detection, Classification, and Location in Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Modern power systems require advanced techniques to detect, classify, and locate faults efficiently. This study explores the use of Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for fault detection location identification and type of fault (Symmetrical and unsymmetrical) faults. ANFIS, combining neural networks and fuzzy logic, can handle the complexities and uncertainties of power system faults. By training on historical data, ANFIS accurately identifies different fault types and pinpoints their locations. Simulation results show its effectiveness in terms of accuracy and speed, making it a valuable tool for improving power system reliability and reducing downtime. Future work will focus on real-time implementation and integration with other smart grid technologies to further enhance fault management capabilities.

articleTitle: Hybrid PWM Control for Speed Control of Induction Motor with Improved Performance of Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper provides a detailed examination of speed control methods for induction motors, with a specific focus on the use of different pulse width modulation (PWM) techniques to achieve precise speed regulation and efficient motor operation. The study investigates the application of sinusoidal PWM (SPWM), third harmonic injection PWM (THPWM), space vector PWM (SVPWM), and selective harmonic elimination PWM (SHEPWM). The proposed hybrid PWM technique is analyzed and compared with existing PWM techniques in both open-loop and closed-loop control strategies. The incorporation of feedback mechanisms such as speed sensors to dynamically adjust the PWM signals has been considered. Through the adjustment of carrier signal frequency and modulation index, the study identifies the optimal PWM technique for minimizing total harmonic distortion (THD) and switching losses. The paper concludes with recommendations on the most effective PWM techniques for specific conditions.

articleTitle: Leveraging Virtual Synchronous Generators for Stable Wind Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The integration of wind energy into modern power systems has introduced significant challenges to maintaining grid stability due to the reduced inertia of inverter-based wind energy systems. To address these challenges, the concept of Virtual Synchronous Generators (VSGs) has emerged as a promising solution. VSG with Hardware in loop (HIL) technology emulates the behavior of synchronous generators, enhancing the dynamic performance of the grid by providing synthetic inertia and damping. This study investigates the application of VSGs for improving transient stability in wind-integrated power systems. The Equal Area Criterion (EAC) is utilized as an analytical tool to assess the system's transient stability under various operating conditions and fault scenarios. By simulating wind energy integration with VSG control, the study demonstrates significant improvements in critical clearing times and the ability to maintain system synchronization during transient disturbances. Additionally, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is employed to optimize power generation, ensuring the wind turbine operates at its maximum capacity under varying wind conditions. The results underline the efficacy of VSGs in enhancing the stability margin of renewable-rich power grids, thereby supporting the reliable and resilient integration of wind energy. This work provides valuable insights into the design and implementation of VSG-based control strategies for next-generation power systems.

articleTitle: A Complementary FET (CFET)-Based NAND Design to Reduce RC Delay
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: As semiconductor innovation proceeds to scale down, minimizing delays caused by resistance (R) and capacitance (C) in coordinate's circuits gets to be pivotal for moving forward execution. This work proposes a Complementary FET (CFET)-based NAND plan to decrease RC delay in rationale circuits. Conventional CMOS-based plans endure from expanded RC delay due to parasitic capacitances and resistances, particularly as gadget measurements recoil. The CFET design, which coordinating both n-type and p-type transistors in a single gadget, offers a one-of-a-kind arrangement by moving forward drive current, lessening exchanging control, and upgrading generally speed compared to routine CMOS rationale. In this, we show a novel CFET-based NAND entryway that addresses the RC delay by optimizing the resistance and capacitance characteristics through gadget scaling and format procedures. Recreations uncover a noteworthy diminishment in engendering delay and control utilization compared to standard CMOS NAND plans. The CFET-based plan illustrates predominant execution in terms of both speed and vitality productivity, making it a promising candidate for future high-performance rationale circuits. This work gives profitable experiences into the potential of CFETs for overcoming the challenges postured by RC delay in progressed VLSI plans.

articleTitle: Analysis of VSC-HVDC System in the Asynchronously Operating Grids During AC Line Faults
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The growing energy demand and ruler electrification accelerates the integration of synchronously and asynchronously operating grids. Generation based on hydro, wind or solar may operate at a frequency slightly different than the national grid due to its intermittent nature and operational constraints. It is important to integrate the generation of various sources to improve grid reliability. Wind energy farms are usually integrated into the grid using VSC (voltage source converters)-HVDC systems. Faults on either side of the HVDC link may create operational and stability issues for interconnecting the HVDC link. The fault ride-through is the ability of the VSC-HVDC system to remain connected with the grid during faults. This paper explores and analyzes the fault ride-through ability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{a}\pm \mathbf{100}\ \mathbf{kV}$</tex>, 200 MW two-level VSC-HVDC to maintain interconnections between grids, especially during the presence of intermittent sources like wind farms at one end of the VSC-HVDC system.

articleTitle: Robust Current Control in Lithium-Ion Battery with a Bidirectional Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a bidirectional buck-boost converter for effective lithium-ion battery energy management. The primary objective is to ensure consistent of charging and discharging currents, which are very important for maintaining the long life and performance of the battery system. A proportional-integral (PI) current controller is employed to regulate the energy flow, enabling precise current control during both the charging and discharging cycles. Detailed MATLAB simulations are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed system and demonstrating the PI controller's capability to maintain stable output current under operating conditions. The implementation of the bidirectional converter, combined with the PI control strategy, offers a reliable approach to optimizing lithium-ion battery better performance, enhancing system stability, and ensuring efficient energy utilization in energy storage systems. This work provides valuable insights into the integration of advanced control techniques for improved battery energy management in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Assisted DC Microgrid Voltage Regulation Using Multipoint Droop Control Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In a standalone DC microgrids, there should be balance between electricity supply and demand in real-time in order to maintain the system voltage. Energy storage management system plays an important role in fulfilling the demand-supply requirement to achieve this power balance. Energy storage management system can help the system to regulate the bus voltage. Droop control mechanisms used to manage storage elements like super-capacitor can improve voltage regulation. Supercapacitors have high rate of charging/discharging, high-power density, fast response, good efficiency and have long lifetime in energy conversion which make it suitable for high power applications. In this paper, a control scheme using multipoint droop control for a DC microgrid (MG) is proposed. The super-capacitor operates in charge or discharge modes based on certain specific voltage bandwidths over multipoint droop characteristics. The objective of the proposed control scheme is to maintain the DC bus voltage within a specified tolerance level and support current sharing among all the converters in the system.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Hydrogen Production Rate Control for a PEM Electrolyzer Load Using PID Controller Supplied from a Small-scale Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive voltage control approach for the green hydrogen production flow rate from a Proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer supplied through a small-scale microgrid system. For this purpose, the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller is utilized. The hydrogen production rate from an electrolyzer depends upon the current supplied to the electrolyzer system. Hence, to regulate the hydrogen production rate, it is essential to regulate the current provided for the electrolysis process while controlling the input voltage to the electrolyzer voltage. This electrolyzer is connected through a DC-DC buck converter and supplied by a small-scale microgrid system. The considered microgrid system is powered by a solar PV and battery storage unit to supply a DC electrolyzer load connected through a buck converter and an AC load connected through a single-phase inverter. The results are checked for variations in irradiance levels of solar and controller performance is observed using various performance indices (PIs). For the study, the solar irradiance corresponds to the Roorkee area situated in Uttarakhand state of India (coordinates 29.8543° <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>, 77.8880° <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>) is considered. The proposed control approach is validated through extensive simulations under MATLAB/Simulink®environment.

articleTitle: Binary Artemisinin Optimization Algorithm for Optimal Phasor Measurement Unit Placement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: For wide area control and monitoring of power systems, for obtaining the real-time data Phasor measurement units are used. These devices play a vital role in power systems to measure the phasor values of voltage and current. It is essential to arrange the position of the PMUs at optimal locations with the minimum number of units and as well as maintaining the grid observability. This paper proposes the new Binary Artemisinin Optimization (BAO) method, a meta-heuristic algorithm that is influenced by the Artemisinin malaria treatment Protocol. For the optimum PMU placement problem, the proposed method is superior for finding the optimum locations and the number of PMUs needed to be minimum while maintaining the grid observability. To find the best Strategy for PMU Placement under normal conditions for 14,30, and 57 IEEE benchmark systems and these test systems are simulated in MATLAB. The proposed outcome results are compared with the existing methods such as Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), Teaching-Learning Based Optimization (TLBO), Binary Linear Programming (BILP), and Branch and Bound Algorithm. The results are more precise, fast convergence, and obtain fewer iterations.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Improved Linear Sinusoidal Tracer Controlled Single-Stage and Dual-Stage Three-Phase Grid-Tied PV System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper compares single-stage and dual-stage Improved Linear Sinusoidal Tracer (ILST) based three-phase grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) systems. These systems facilitate the integration of solar energy into grid while improving the power quality of the distribution network. This design incorporates Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT), PV power injection into the grid, harmonic reduction at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC), and grid current balancing. Both single-stage and dual-stage configurations utilize a three-phase voltage source converter (VSC) controlled by an ILST algorithm. The single-stage and dual-stage systems are modeled and simulated using MATLAB. This ILST control algorithm of grid-tied PV system helps to maintain Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of PCC voltages and grid currents within prescribed limits.

articleTitle: Digital Optimization Process of Thermal Trip Unit in Circuit Breakers for Carbon Footprint Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Circuit Breakers are major components of protection systems, which also contributes significantly towards scope-3 greenhouse gas emission. Inside a circuit breaker, the thermal trip unit or a bimetallic strip contributes significantly towards watt-loss. Different bimetals exhibit different structural and thermal behavior and hence, a common framework to optimize bimetal for circuit breakers is required. A breaker is also expected to operate at different constraints laid under UL489 standard. Experimental, numerical, and statistical methods are used to reduce overall watt-loss of a breaker. In this study, an electrical and thermal resistance network modelling methodology is highlighted to optimize the thermal trip unit. This model is verified with thermal test and simulation data. Statistical design exploration and watt-loss optimization is also highlighted. Optimum bimetal design shows ~35% reduction in overall watt-loss, which may give significant benefit in reducing overall carbon footprint. The same optimization process can be used to improve efficiency and reduce carbon emission of circuit breakers of different size and rating.

articleTitle: Energy Management of Grid Connected PV System without Energy Storage Using High Gain Converter for DC Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The penetration of conventional energy sources is decreasing while energy demand is increasing. Therefore, alternative energy sources are required to ensure an emission-free environment and to meet energy demands, such as photovoltaic (PV) systems. The generating voltage of a PV source is low, so high-voltage gain converters have been developed to meet the required load demands. This article presents a grid-connected PV system using a high-gain converter. The high-gain converter in the proposed system offers several advantages, such as fewer components, design with a single switch, minimal gate driver circuitry, low cost, and high efficiency. The PV source voltage acts as the input to this high-gain converter. The bidirectional DC/AC converter is controlled by hysteresis current control. The active component current for hysteresis current control is generated using the loss component current, load power, and PV power. The aforementioned control strategy maintains power management between the electrical sources and the load. The suggested system is simulated for a 1.2 kW power rating, and the obtained simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Enhanced Grid Stability of Bi-Directional Converter in Grid to Vehicle System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The integration of Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) systems is critical for the sustainable integration of electric vehicles (EVs) with modern power grids. These systems enable bidirectional energy flow, allowing efficient EV charging in G2V mode and feeding stored energy back to the grid in V2G mode, particularly during peak demand. A bidirectional buck-boost converter regulates the voltage, ensuring safe and efficient energy transfer. G2V and V2G systems contribute to grid stability, load balancing, and optimized utilization of renewable energy sources, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and carbon emissions. Future advancements in power electronics and real-time smart grid integration will enhance their effectiveness, necessitating further research on their impact on grid stability and resilience.

articleTitle: Power Management in Photovoltaic Based Microgrid Under Varying Load and Generations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The incorporation of Renewable Energy sources (RES) into power system is becoming more widespread due to the global trend towards sustainable energy. The potential for RES to minimize carbon emissions and improve energy sustainability is enormous. As RES is intermittent, it becomes challenging to maintain the system stable and reliable. This paper aims for effective power management in a renewable rich microgrid using photovoltaic (PV) system as dispatchable source to satisfy load demand under various operating conditions to maintain system stability. A three-bus low-voltage microgrid system is used in this work as a test system in the MATLAB/Simulink platform to provide efficient power management and an experimental setup for PV system as a dispatchable energy source has been Implemented.

articleTitle: Design and Control of an Improved Four-Phase SRM Drive Using a 4-Level Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The paper presents a novel speed control topology for 4-phase Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs) for EVs. The design is based on a MOSFET-switching enhanced four-level converter providing four-modes of operation which are operated in levels for minimizing the torque ripple. Using MATLAB/SIMULINK Software, an 8/6 4-phase SRM is simulated using the proposed converter and controller, the controller here is a closed loop control of voltage PWM SRM drive with an inner current loop. The simulation data validated the torque ripple-reducing capability of the suggested converter in the SRM control process. Based on simulation outcomes a comparative analysis is performed.

articleTitle: Modeling and Monthly Maximum Power Analysis of Solar Photovoltaic Modules in Dhanbad Using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents a photovoltaic array model for tracking maximum power points and analyzing monthly power variations, incorporating solar irradiation and temperature effects. The analysis shows peak power generation in June and the lowest in December, correlating with environmental patterns. The model offers valuable insights for optimizing PV system performance, aiding researchers and manufacturers in enhancing efficiency under diverse conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of DPC Techniques Used in DFIG Based WECS
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Direct Power Control (DPC) has become a widely researched technique for controlling Doubly Fed Induction Machine (DFIM) based Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS). The control operation of DPC during grid voltage imbalance, voltage dip, and non-constant switching frequency has been an area of significant interest for many researchers. This paper presents a selective analysis of recent studies on the DPC of DFIM with the aim of identifying gaps in the current literature. The paper focused on three aspects: optimization techniques used in control blocks, performance evaluation parameters, and parameters of AI models used. It is observed that more research attention is needed on the estimation block using AI techniques other than Fuzzy and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). Additionally, real-time performance analysis through hardware implementation of WECS is necessary, and the evaluation of other parameters besides Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and power ripple reduction is critical in assessing the performance of proposed control strategies. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into potential areas for further research aimed at improving the performance and robustness of DPC control of DFIM-based WECS.

articleTitle: Advanced Epileptic Seizure Recognition with a Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Model on EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Epileptic seizure recognition (ESR) is a vital area in healthcare, neurology, and patient monitoring, particularly for managing epilepsy in real time. While deep learning (DL) models have shown exceptional performance in recognizing seizures from EEG signals, processing sequential and time-series data remains challenging. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework combining one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks to enhance seizure recognition. The 1D CNN efficiently captures localized temporal features from EEG data, while the BiLSTM models bidirectional long-range dependencies, improving temporal feature representation. Tested on a benchmark dataset, the model achieves an outstanding accuracy of 98.18%, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. These results underscore the effectiveness of integrating CNN for feature extraction and BiLSTM for sequence modeling, offering a robust and reliable approach for automated ESR in clinical applications.

articleTitle: EV Battery Charging with a Solar-Integrated Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This study presents the battery charging of an Electric Vehicle (EV) system with a boost converter designed for charging from Solar Photovoltaic Cells (SPV). It has been established that the incorporation of these sources seeks to improve energy usage, minimize the dependency of non-renewable resources and also improve the general charging systems. This EV charging system consists in the SPV array and the boost converter. Depending on availability of renewable energy, it regulates the flow of energy and also charge EV batteries. A Boost converter's is used while charging the EV battery using solar power for extraction of the optimum SPVpower. This supply is produced by boost converter that also operates with the PFC circuit. Simulation is performed in MATLAB for the suggested system with the help of different operating conditions in order to measure its performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Monitoring and Controlling the Electrical Parameters in Industrial Applications Using IoT Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The proposed system will introduce an IoT-based smart energy monitoring solution to enhance real-time tracking and management of electrical parameters, using the ESP32 Wi-Fi module as the core processing unit. The system integrates current and voltage sensors for accurate measurement of electricity consumption. These sensors capture electrical parameters processed and calibrated by the ESP32 so that power usage and energy consumption can be considered in their calculation. The processed data is then transmitted to the cloud, where users can now monitor and control their energy consumption using the Blynk mobile application. For example, this innovative system features live monitoring of electrical parameters, customizable alerts for abnormal consumption, and remote device control via relay module. These are then integrated into the system, which is useful in the management of energy for residential and commercial purposes, thus contributing to the conservation of energy that promotes sustainability and sound energy practice.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization Approach for EV Hosting Capacity Maximization of Distribution Networks with Renewable Generations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The increasing integration of electric vehicle (EV) loads and renewable-based generators in distribution networks necessitates the evaluation of EV hosting capacity (EVHC) of distribution networks in presence of renewable generations for their stable and reliable operations. EVHC of a network is defined as the maximum amount of EV load that can be accommodated by a network without violating its operational limits. This paper presents a multi-objective optimization approach to maximize EVHC of distribution networks with renewable generations. Minimization of total cost of placement of renewable-based generators including cost of energy loss and maximization of EVHC of distribution networks are considered as the optimization objectives. Pareto-dominance principle-based multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) is used to determine a set of non-dominated solutions which clearly show that the considered objectives are conflicting with each other. The proposed approach is validated on 33-bus distribution network.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Boost Converter Design for PV Systems Using P&O MPPT
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The use of renewable energy has become popular due to the effect's fossil fuels have on the environment and their scarcity. Temperature, voltage across the array's terminals, and radiation all affect the output power of solar photovoltaic systems. This work proposes an enhance fixed step-size Perturb & Observe (P&O) Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT). This widely used MPPT approach record the change in electrical energy by perturbing the operating point of the PV array. Tracking a photovoltaic module's excellent power point can increase solar energy conversion efficiency. This study uses a DC-DC Boost converter to simulate and produce an 859 W solar photo-voltaic array connected with an external resistive load P&O MPPT approach. Result provides the 99.9% power efficiency; therefore, overall system efficiency is more significant and indicating good performance.

articleTitle: DC-DC Cascode Converter-Based Speed Control of PMBLDC Motors for EV Drive Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a DC-DC cascode buck-boost converter-based speed control of permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) motors. The control scheme consists of a voltage source inverter (VSI) that is controlled by a commutation logic developed from signals of hall effect sensors. The output voltage of the cascode converter is controlled by a proportional-integral (PI) controller. The primary objective of utilizing this DC-DC cas-code converter is to achieve high voltage gain, thereby improving efficiency by minimizing switching losses. The simulation results show that the proposed control system achieves accurate speed tracking and stable torque performance, even with a sudden increase in speed and torque. The torque profile, back EMF, and speed tracking demonstrate the motor's robustness under real-world conditions, making it suitable for electric vehicles (EVs), The proposed scheme presents a cost-effective solution for PMBLDC motor drives, which require high performance at a relatively low cost. Consequently, it offers a promising alternative for low-power drives, particularly in electric vehicles, robotics, and household appliances.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Impedance Network-Based Cascaded Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper describes the design along with an analysis of a Z-Source or impedance-source-based cascaded MLI for adoption in online UPS applications. The motive of this study is to build a dc-to-ac converter that is utilized for UPS to the load side without stoppage of power and with a step-up output voltage. This is accomplished by feeding CHB-Multilevel circuits through a front-side Z-source unit. Z-source-based MLIs have boosting capabilities and achieve waveforms that are almost sinusoidal. The Z-source unit uses a distinctive impedance circuit to link the converter's main circuit to the power supply, thus the proposed converter provides properties, such as shoot-through state, that are unattainable in conventional inverters. In contrast to conventional inverters, Z-source-based MLIs are more reliable and credible for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) applications. The proposed converter's performance is assessed analytically by varying the shoot-through duty ratio, and MATLAB/SIMULINK is used to simulate and validate the results. The inverter switches are controlled by implementing shoot-through control along with Standard Phase Shifted Pulse Width Modulation (PS-SPWM). The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed converter control using PS-SPWM along with shoot-through exhibits higher voltage utilisation and a lower power squander compared to the conventional SPWM inverter. The simulation results have been discussed by employing Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis shows higher gain and better performance compared to the conventional topologies.

articleTitle: Application of Double Stack Magneto-Resistance Sensor for Angular Measurements at Joints in a Two-Link Bipedal Robot
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents the application of double stack magneto-resistance sensor (DSMRS) in a two-link bipedal robot. A non-linear magnetic transducer-Double stack TMR sensor, is used for the detection of accurate movement of robot. A direct digital interface and their methodology is discussed in order to find the accurate joint angle for two-link biped robot. The SPICE based simulation and experimental based study is carried out to analyze the effectiveness of device. The interface parameters like standard deviation, signal to noise ratio, enob and repeatability error are calculated.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Battery Management System for Li-Ion Type EVs with Predictive Control and FPGA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The increasing acceptance of electric vehicles (EVs) shows the significance of efficient and reliable battery management systems (BMS) for ensuring safety, optimizing the performance, and extend battery life. Various BMS algorithms exists in literature. Model Predictive Control (MPC) is a powerful tool due to its ability to handle multi-variable control processes and incorporate system constraints has also been considered for BMS design. Further, with the high computational demands of MPC, Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) are also being integrated to enhance real-time processing capabilities, making BMS solutions for lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries more effective. In recent times, the Li-ion batteries are considered to be the most suitable for EVs. This fiat has resulted from many years of research and development that improved Li-ion's performance in comparison to Lead-acid, Nickel, Sodium based batteries. Despite these advantages, still there exists some key challenges in terms of safety, cost-effectiveness, longevity, recycling, and degradation. To adhere these concerns, BMS is used in the EVs for proper use of the Li-ion batteries that reduces number of charging and discharging cycles, estimates various health parameters of the battery such as state-of-charge (SoC), state-of-health (SoH), regulates the cell temperature, and computes the degradation. This paper reviews recent advances in BMS using MPC and FPGA, assessing developments in modeling, control strategies, hardware implementation, and testing frameworks. Innovations that address the challenges of state estimation, fault detection, and system efficiency are emphasized for current research and future directions.

articleTitle: FinFET Technology Based Development of Energy Efficient Datapath System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In today's electronics industry, extensive research is dedicated to advancing nanoscale VLSI designs, particularly focusing on energy-efficient solutions. N anoscale designs often exhibit elevated power consumption due to the close proximity of source and drain regions within these diminutive devices. The limited channel space between source and drain weakens channel control, resulting in increased leakage currents. The FinFET device emerges as a prime candidate for contemporary electronic circuits, offering enhanced performance. This study is centered on the implementation of FinFET technology-based data paths, emphasizing low-power and high-speed capabilities. The data path assumes a crucial role in executing logical and arithmetic operations within the system, encompassing essential functions like NOT, AND, OR, and more. A 4-bit carry-look-ahead adder is employed for bitwise arithmetic tasks such as addition, subtraction, increment, and decrement. The designs are realized using the L T -Spice simulator, showcasing notable achievements. The proposed design significantly reduces power consumption, cutting the propagation delay by 9 µsee compared to CMOS technology, which consumed 4.7 µW. The findings strongly indicate that FinFET-based data paths outperform bulk CMOS technology, reinforcing their potential for superior performance and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control for a Hybrid Energy Storage based Low Voltage DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) that include batteries and supercapacitors are now widely used in DC microgrids to manage energy fluctuations. In this paper, a controller for voltage regulation in a photovoltaic DC microgrid with HESS is proposed. The controller's inner current loop is based on a proportional integral controller, while the outer voltage loop is based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC). The overall current reference for storage systems is generated by the ADRC voltage controller and thereafter distributed to every storage device via a low-pass filter. The anticipated DC bus voltage and total disturbances are estimated using a linear Extended State Observer (ESO). When fast change loads are connected, the ADRC employs a double filter technique to even out battery charging and discharging. The proposed controller's effectiveness and response speed have been validated through simulations using MATLAB/ SIMULINK, and the results are compared to those of a traditional cascaded PI controller. The findings with the proposed controller based on time domain specifications like overshoot and setting time with value 0.13V and 20ms respectively which indicate that the new controller outperforms the conventional one in terms of disturbance resistance and dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Multi Winding Isolated Converter with Cascaded MLI for Solar Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This article proposes application of multi winding Isolated converter using asymmetrical cascaded multilevel Inverter (MLI) for solar electric vehicle. A 9 level MLI is getting multiple DC inputs by the help of a multi secondary winding Flyback converter from a single solar panel. The MLI provides higher level voltage output, which can run the AC motor used in Electric Vehicle (EV) with improved power quality without bulky filter circuits. The secondary windings turn of the converter maintain a ratio of 1:3 to generate 9 level voltage output. The use of MLI reduces the output voltage THD (Total Harmonic distortion) which lies below the set value by IEEE-519 standard. The simulation results of the proposed scheme has validated the theoretical concept.

articleTitle: Optimal Location and Sizing of Distributed Generation Using Horse Herd Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of the Horse Herd Optimisation (HHO) algorithm in the analysis of the optimal sizing of DG units in the distribution system. As more Distributed Generation (DG) is incorporated into power distribution networks, proper sizing and location of DG units is important for improving system performance. HHO algorithm derived from the herd behavior and self-organizing characteristics of horses is used for proper positioning and dimensioning of Distributed Generation units in order to minimize loss and improve voltage profile. HHO is better than conventional PSO methods in terms of exploration-exploitation trade-off making it more appropriate for complex optimization. The performance of the proposed method is tested on the IEEE 33-bus test system in MATLAB. This research confirms HHO as an effective meta heuristic for DG optimization and opens the way for more effective and reliable power systems.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement of Switched Reluctance Motor Using Different PFC Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this paper, a PFC (Power factor correction) converter is designed to improve the power quality of a midpoint converter-based switching reluctance motor (SRM) drive. Low power factor is extremely high harmonic content are produced at the ac mains by a traditional bridge rectifier with a midpoint converter-based SRM drive. The power factor at single-phase AC mains with minimal current harmonics is enhanced by the suggested PFC converter with a midway converter-supplied SRM drive. Additionally, it the proposed topology offers balanced capacitor voltages and a steady DC link voltage. The Matlab/Simulink environment is used to model and simulate the operation of this SRM drive with an input of a PFC converter. Additionally, the PFC converter performance contrasts with traditional diode bridge rectifier converters for SRM drives.

articleTitle: Design of Highly Efficient Switched Reluctance Motor for Heavy Duty Exhaust Fan for Air Ventilation System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: A wide variety of motors are present in market for air ventilation system but those are dominated by squirrel cage induction motor. Induction motor has lesser efficiencies in FHP motors. For increasing the efficiency permanent magnet motors like BLDC and PMSM are introduced but they involve the assembly of costly magnets which makes the motor expensive and they have thermal limitations. Switched Reluctance Motor, on the one hand, is more efficient than the Induction Motors as they work on the principle of reluctance torque and doesn't incorporate any rotor bars thus reducing the rotor copper loss. On the other hand, they also do not use magnets thus they have no thermal limitations. This research paper proposes Switched Reluctance Motor with 12 stator poles and 10 rotor poles configuration with efficiency greater than 94% for heavy duty exhaust fan application.

articleTitle: Battery-Ultracapacitor based Hybrid Energy System for Electric Vehicle Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Electric Vehicles are becoming more and more popular due to their affordability and renewability, but the Li-ion battery life-span that powers them needs to be improved. This experimental study proposes a way of increasing the lifespan of Li-ion battery by using Hybrid Energy System. In this system the BLDC motor is run by battery in steady state running condition but the energy source is switched to ultracapacitor during transient. This approach is to combine the hybrid system with BLDC motor and emulate its run condition according to Indian Driving Cycle(IDC). At starting for a few seconds the starting current is 67.2A and characteristics demonstrate that the BLDC motor draws a huge current during transient and it can be switched to ultracapacitor during transient in order to save Battery's Ampere-Hour. This findings offers potential applications of Hybrid Energy System for Electric Vehicles in future. The transient data are observed and stored using Mixed Signal Oscilloscope.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Current Control of Induction Motor Drive Integrated with Inverse Rotor Time Constant Estimator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In induction motor (IM) drives, rotor resistance tends to vary significantly due to temperature changes during prolonged operation of drives. Rotor resistance variation can degrade the motor performance, making it crucial to accurately estimate the rotor resistance/rotor time constant to maintain optimal control and achieve high-performance operation. Nowadays, model predictive control (MPC) has gained significant popularity due to its rapid dynamic response and precise control capabilities over the indirect rotor field-oriented control (IRFOC) of IM drives. In this work, a robust model predictive current control (MPCC) scheme for IM drive integrated with inverse rotor time constant estimator has been designed. However, similar to IRFOC, the MPCC scheme is also limited by its dependency on the rotor resistance of the machine, which affects the accuracy of the calculation of slip speed. Thus, in the proposed work, a reactive power (Q) based model reference adaptive system (MRAS) has been incorporated with MPCC scheme to estimate the inverse rotor time constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{r})$</tex>, which makes the MPCC scheme robust against the parameter variation. The proposed work for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\gamma}$</tex> estimation approach ensures precise current control and quicker responses to variations in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{r}$</tex> as compared to the IRFOC. The effectiveness of the proposed MPCC algorithm integrated with an inverse rotor time constant estimator for estimation of inverse rotor time constant in both motoring and generating modes of operation is validated through simulation in MATLAB®/Simulink.

articleTitle: Short-Term Forecasting of Wind Power Plant Generation Based on Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The current excessive exploitation of fossil energy sources has led to skyrocketing prices and significant environmental challenges, including greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. In response, there is an increasing focus on renewable energy sources as viable alternatives to fossil fuels. Among these alternatives, wind energy is particularly noteworthy due to its unlimited availability, cost-effectiveness, and minimal environmental impact. Two critical factors that influence wind energy generation are wind speed and direction, both of which tend to be inherently unstable. To address this, machine learning algorithms have been developed for forecasting wind energy in the contemporary technological landscape. This forecasting process leverages historical data to predict future outcomes. This paper will specifically examine machine learning techniques—Support Vector Regression (SVR), Linear Regression (LR), and Random Forest Regression (RFR)—to predict wind power using weather data as input. The results from these prediction models, developed with a 4-day forecast at 1-day intervals, will be compared against actual results from preceding periods. All methodologies and visualizations will be implemented using Python and Visual Studio Code software.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Off-board Fast Charging DC-DC Converter Regulated by Fuzzy Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: with the shift toward clean energy sources, battery charging for electric vehicles is becoming increasingly significant, especially with the growing focus on clean energy use. A primary challenge in EV charging is reducing charging time. Fast charging, paired with an effective DC-DC converter, addresses this issue. Achieving optimal performance requires a suitable controller for the converter. This paper outlines the design process of a Fuzzy Logic Controller for the DC-DC converter in EV charging applications. The proposed controller is a precise and reliable approach for the system in focus. MATLAB simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the designed constant controller for fast EV charging applications.

articleTitle: Streamer Dynamics in Micro-Contaminated Transformer Oil
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The investigation of microparticles' effect on the electric field, space charge density, and streamer dynamics in transformer oil is crucial for understanding its insulating performance. Microparticles create localized distortions in the electric field leading to early streamer inception, increased propagation velocity and more branching. Additionally, the microparticles influence the space charge density by acting as sites for charge accumulation.
