This uneven distribution of space charge alters the surrounding electric field, contributing to more complex streamer behavior. As the space charge build around the particles, it leads to stronger field gradients, which produces more streamer branches and reduce the dielectric strength of the oil. The combined effects of enhanced electric field distortion and space charge accumulation significantly lower the breakdown voltage of transformer oil, making it more prone to electrical failure. Using COMSOL Multiphysics, this study simulates how microparticles alter these key properties under high-voltage conditions.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Different Controllers for DC Bus Voltage Control in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The present scenario in power system is demanding a large number of micro-sources derived from renewable energy and battery storage. Moreover, electronic loads and EV technologies are evolving at a great pace. DC microgrids (DCMG) are found to be more effective for their integration into the system because of reduced converter count and control complexity. The basic variable quantity in focus here is the DC bus voltage whose stability determines and ensures the safe and reliable operation of the DCMG. The stability is achieved with the help of controllers deployed within these micro-sources. The sources considered in the studied DCMG are PV, PMSG-Wind turbine, battery, and AC grid. The proposed work provides the relative study of five different types of controllers - proportional-integral, model predictive controller, sliding mode controller, fuzzy logic controller, and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system. These controllers are incorporated in the outer loop control of the grid side converter to regulate the DBV. The effectiveness of the proposed control is validated through simulation in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Comparative Impact Assessement of Energy Storage Systems on Frequency Regulation with Various Operating Strategies under ABT
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper investigates the comparative impact assessment of energy storage systems on frequency regulation with various operating strategies under Availability Based Tariff in an isolated power system having generation from thermal, wind and wave energy sources along with various energy storage systems(ESS) — Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage (SMES), Supercapacitor Energy Storage (SCES), Redox Flow Battery (RFB), and Flywheel Energy Storage — for mitigating frequency deviations. Simulation studies in MATLAB/Simulink were conducted to evaluate key performance under dynamic operating conditions. Results reveal that SMES and RFB exhibit relatively better response with minimal overshoot (≤ 0.001 Hz), negligible undershoot, and least instantaneous settling time, making them appropriate for rapid frequency stabilization. SCES also demonstrates effective performance, albeit with slight oscillations due to its slower discharge rate. The analysis emphasizes the critical role of ESS technologies in enhancing the frequency regulation under different operating strategies under ABT. This study provides insights into the preliminary selection and integration of ESS in modern power systems, contributing to the reliable and stable grid operations amidst increasing renewable energy penetration.

articleTitle: Binary Educational Competition Optimizer (BECO) Algorithm For Optimum PMU Placement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In power systems, for wide area monitoring and controlling of various electrical parameters, Phasor Measurement units are used. These devices play a vital role and the measured parameters are time-synchronized through the utilization of the global positioning system. But these PMUs are more expensive. Due to this expensiveness, optimum sites for placing PMUs to obtain maximum observability, and finding a minimal number of PMUs is mandatory. This paper proposes the novel Binary Educational Competition Optimizer (BECO) algorithm inspired by the various educational institutions, to identify the best positions. The proposed approach is simulated for 14, 30, and 57-bus IEEE benchmark systems. The suggested approach results fulfill the optimum locations of the PMU placement with complete visibility of the grid and obtain the minimal number of PMUs. These simulated test results are analyzed in MATLAB with the existing methods such as fast convergence and obtaining fewer iterations.

articleTitle: Stability Enhancement in Power Systems with High Renewable Penetration: The Role of Grid-Forming Inverters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: As power systems integrate increasing levels of renewable energy sources (RES), stability becomes a significant challenge due to the unique dynamic characteristics of inverter-based resources (IBRs) like solar and wind. This paper examines stability issues in renewable-dominated grids, focusing on voltage and transient stability. A test system based on real-world renewable energy complexes is used to assess the impact of IBR penetration under various contingencies. Simulations reveal that grid-following (GFL) inverters struggle in low short-circuit ratio (SCR) systems, causing voltage dips, delayed active power recovery, and post-disturbance oscillations. In contrast, grid-forming (GFM) inverters improve system response, mitigating voltage instability and enhancing reactive power support. The study highlights the critical role of GFM deployment in enhancing grid resilience, providing key insights for operators and planners to manage renewable integration more effectively.

articleTitle: Multi Objective Power Optimization in DC mi Crogrid Using Hybrid GA-PSO Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Renewable energy resources are viable and trustworthy solutions for ensuring timely and universal access to power. The solar photovoltaic (PV) system stands out among them, due to sun radiation, cell performance, and ambient temperatures, its output power varies. Also, the modules used typically convert less efficiently. In light of this, the deployment of maximum power point monitoring becomes an absolute need in order to maximize the amount of energy that can be harvested from the sun and to improve the overall efficiency of solar systems. This work gives a comparative analysis of maximum power point tracking utilizing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and hybrid Genetic and Particle Swarm Optimization algorithms (GA-PSO) approaches. In addition, a microgrid that incorporates a solar PV cell and a battery system has been constructed in MATLAB. During the course of this investigation, a comparison of the output power with various changing input factors, such as irradiation and temperature, was carried out.

articleTitle: Speed Control of 3 Phase Induction Motors using Different PWM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Induction motors are widely favored for their reliability, affordability, and durability. While traditionally not capable of variable speed operation, recent advancements in speed control methods have made them ubiquitous in electrical drives. Out of the several methods of speed control of an induction motor the constant V/f speed control method is most widely used. This approach maintains a constant V/f ratio to keep the magnetizing flux stable, ensuring the torque remains consistent. Implementing V/f control involves modeling a PWM inverter feeding into the induction motor drive. MATLAB and Simulink were used to demonstrate both Open Loop using SPWM and Closed Loop V/f Control using SPWM and SVPWM techniques. Closed-Loop control with a Proportional Integral Controller and SVPWM technique emerged as a superior method for speed control while preserving the torque. Various parameters such as Power Consumption, Line Voltage and Current, Torque, Slip and Speed were thoroughly analyzed across these models.

articleTitle: Impact of Material Variations on Gate-All-Around Nanowire FETs for Low-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The present research resolves scaling problems in advanced technology nodes by designing and analyzing high-k dielectric Gate-All-Around (GAA) silicon nanowire Field-Effect Transistors (FETs). GAA FETs are ideal for sub-5 nm nodes because they offer superior electrostatic control and less short-channel effects than conventional planar and FinFET designs. The ability of high-k dielectrics, such SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, to achieve maximum gate capacitance while minimizing leakage currents is being studied. Subthreshold swing (SS) and drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) are significantly improved in GAA FETs with HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> through careful tuning of device design, including channel length and nanowire diameter, as the study shows. These improvements show how GAA designs and high-k materials may be employed to enhance device performance and scalability.

articleTitle: Analysis of ADRC with Complex Pole and Design of ESO Based SMC
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Nowadays, challenges in load frequency control (LFC) are increasing to consider various non-linearity in the system. To deal with disturbance in the LFC system active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is a popular approach. Linear ADRC fails successfully to deal with non-linearity in the system. A robust control technique using sliding mode controller (SMC) which effectively deal with uncertainty of the system is proposed. In this paper, an SMC with full order extended state observer (ESO) is designed. The controller and observer gains are obtained using pole placement technique and is used to design the SMC. The observer-based SMC is investigated for single area non-reheat system without and with non-linearity like generation rate constraint (GRC) and governor dead band (GDB). The parameter of the non-linear ESO i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha= 0.1, \delta= 0. 1$</tex> gives the best response for non-reheat LFC system whereas <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha=0.5$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta=0.1$</tex> gives the best response for the reheat system.

articleTitle: Frequency Control Management in Interconnected Islanded Port Incorporating Nonlinear Control Strategy with Cogeneration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The performance of interconnected microgrids is investigated in this study with particular focus paid to load balancing, frequency administration, and grid stability. A shipboard microgrid and a marine microgrid are the two distinct isolated microgrid systems under study. Archimedes Wave Energy Conversion, Tidal Power Generation, and Photovoltaic Energy are examples of renewable energy sources that are a part of the maritime microgrid. Along with adjustable loads like freezers and heat pumps, it also contains controlled generations like Micro Hydro Turbine Generators and Biodiesel Generation Units. In area 1, a battery energy storage system serves as a backup. In addition to controlled generation such as micro hydro turbine generators and biodiesel generating units, the shipboard microgrid consists of geothermal, wind turbine generators, and solar towers. Additionally, it has controllable loads like freezers and heat pumps, with area-2 backup being Capacitor Energy Storage. Energy storage devices, dynamic loads, and a range of conventional and renewable energy sources define microgrids. A Fractional Order PID controller is used for Load Frequency Control, and it is optimized utilizing the Mountain Gazelle Optimization (MGO), Chimp Optimization Algorithm, and Swarm Optimization algorithms. The MGO algorithm is contrasted with other metaheuristic techniques like CHOA and SO. It is distinguished by its excellent convergence ability and parameter freedom. In comparison to previous optimization strategies, simulation results show how well the MGO-FOPID controller minimizes frequency deviation, area control error, and power fluctuations under a range of load circumstances.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Multi-Phase Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Multi-phase induction motors (MPIMs) provide significant advantages over three-phase induction motors, such as greater power output, reduced torque ripple, enhanced fault tolerance, and increased control flexibility. These features make multiphase drive systems a compelling option for medium and heavy-duty electric vehicle (MHEV) applications. This study focuses specifically on MPIMs, presenting a mathematical model based on vector space decomposition (VSD) technique for MPIMs and generalised this concept for five-phase induction motor (FPIM) drives. Additionally, this paper examines the impact of variable loading conditions on FPIM performance. Simulations were conducted using MATLAB/SIMULINK to develop and analyze the mathematical model under varying load conditions, with results demonstrating the effects of these changes.

articleTitle: Mitigating Cloud Movement Effects on Solar Panel Performance through Different Re-configuration Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) into the grid for reliable and stable operation is witnessing significant growth. Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems are key contributors to enhancing the grid's RES capacity. The Solar PV installed capacity improved by 30 % in 2023. Challenges arise in partially shaded conditions, where some parts of the solar PV array may be obstructed, leading to suboptimal performance of the entire array. Achieving optimal performance in the connected solar PV arrays is essential, typically accomplished by configuring arrays in parallel and/or series to operate at the Maximum Power Point (MPP). This paper explores the application of various metaheuristic methods, including Particle Swarm Optimization, Bald Eagle Search, Manta Ray Foraging Optimization, and Gorilla Troop Optimizer. The study considers complete cloud movement across a 9X9 solar PV array. The movement of the clouds is categorized into 9 different stages of partial shading. The switching of the solar panels is employed to maximize output power under shaded conditions. The results are categorized into dynamic and static reconfiguration. MATLAB is employed for the implementation of these metaheuristic techniques.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Analysis in Hybrid Power System Using Optimized Fractional Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Frequency oscillations in a unified power system remain a critical concern due to load uncertainties. These oscillations are mitigated through the use of controllers. In this work, a fractional mathematics-based Non-Integer Modified PID (NI-Mod-PID) controller is proposed to stabilize frequency oscillations in a hybrid power system integrated with an EV aggregator. The optimal gain parameters for the NI-Mod-PID controllers are determined using the Selfish Herd Optimization (SHO) technique to minimize frequency deviations. To simulate an imbalance between load and generation, a sudden load perturbation of 8% is introduced in the unified power system. The performance of the interconnected system, in terms of tie-line power and frequency oscillations, is assessed using response evaluation metrics such as positive peak, negative peak, and settling time. The superiority of the NI-Mod-PID controller is demonstrated by comparing its results with those of the conventional PID and NIPID controllers. In the later phase, the robustness of the proposed NI-Mod-PID controller is evaluated under unexpected load increases, further establishing its effectiveness and dominance in maintaining system stability.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity High-Frequency Fludic Passive Sensor Using Substrate Integrated Waveguide for Measurement of Glucose Concentration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents a high-sensitivity, high-frequency (HSHF) passive sensor using substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology for the characterization of glucose concentration. The proposed sensor consists of SIW and an elliptical-shaped sensing cavity and is fed by a 50 Ω tapered line. The operating frequency of the sensor is near 7.4 GHz. The resonance of the sensor shifted due to the use of different concentrations of glucose fluid. A small change in glucose concentration gives a larger (0.5 GHz) shift in frequency. The proposed sensor supports the transverse electromagnetic (TE) mode. The sensitivity of the proposed sensor is high due to the transformation of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>mode of SIW into TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf>of sensing cavity mode.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Power of TQWT and Adaptive CNNs for Accurate PQ Disturbance Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Power quality (PQ) disturbances significantly impact the reliability of modern electrical systems, necessitating robust and precise detection methods. This study introduces a novel framework that integrates the Tunable-Q Wavelet Transform (TQWT) and an Adaptive Convolutional Neural Network (Adaptive CNN) for detecting and classifying PQ disturbances with high accuracy. TQWT is employed for multi-resolution signal decomposition, extracting rich features across varying frequency ranges to capture complex disturbances such as interharmonics, transients, sags, and swells. The decomposition parameters, including the Q-factor, redundancy, and number of levels, are dynamically optimized using a Signal-Adaptive Parameterization Algorithm (SAPA). This optimization ensures that the decomposition aligns with the unique characteristics of each PQ disturbance, maximizing feature sparsity and noise resilience. The extracted features are processed through an Adaptive CNN, equipped with a Dynamic Kernel Pooling (DKP) mechanism that adjusts kernel shapes and sizes based on the spectral characteristics of input features. Additionally, a hybrid loss function integrates classification accuracy, feature sparsity, and noise suppression, ensuring robust model training. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the framework's superior performance, achieving high classification accuracy and robustness under noisy conditions.

articleTitle: Solar PV-Based Mobile Phone Battery Charger
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper demonstrates solar PV (SPV) based mobile battery charging architecture employing a power electronics (DC-DC buck type) converter. The perturb and observe MPPT optimization algorithm is used to harvest the utmost power from the SSPV. In the DC-DC (buck) converter, a blocking diode is connected at the output side of the SPV to prevent the reverse current flow from the battery to the battery charger (DC-DC converter). The controller charges the mobile battery in three modes i.e., float charging stage, MPPT bulk charging stage and a steady voltage absorption stage. The studied mobile charging system is analyzed in MATLAB/Simulink environment. To incorporate the partially shading condition in the SPV of the proposed system, the solar irradiance of the SPV is decreased from 1000 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 400 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for the time instance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> = 30 s to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> =40 s. This partial shading condition of the SPV is incorporated to observe the charging performances of the mobile battery by using a mobile battery charger controller. The performance evaluation of the proposed system designed in MATLAB/Simulink is carried out in terms of the dynamic performance of SPV and the mobile battery with charge controller.

articleTitle: Centralized-Decentralized Secondary Controller for Standalone PV-Battery Unit Type Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The encouraging use of renewable sources like solar photovoltaic (PV) for decreasing the dependency on fossil fuel based energy generation has led to realization of microgrids (MGs) on the existing distribution network. The intermittency of PV sources is taken care by storage device like battery. Handling intermittent power generation, proper power sharing among multiple parallel connected PVB systems, accommodating the time-varying load scenarios, shedding of noncritical loads under energy deficient conditions, etc., are some essential control requirements of such a MG system. In this work, a centralized-decentralized secondary controller (CDSC) is proposed for coordinating the operation of an individual PVB units in the MG system. The proposed centralized secondary controller (CSC) evaluates the different settings based on the received information from the local controller (LC). Further, the decentralized secondary controller (DSC) decides the references for the LC based on the information received from the CSC and LC measurements. The developed CDSC considers the actual power extracted from the PV array as well as the charging/discharging current limit constraints of the battery controller that increase the battery life. The proposed control architecture has been extensively tested for different operating scenario on a European distribution network using the PSCAD/EMTDC platform.

articleTitle: Design of PV Based Streetlight Using Solar Radiation Estimation Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this paper, the work is based on real life problem related to streetlight installed in the remote areas. Currently available PV based streetlight is a generalized design for all locations. As the solar radiation pattern is not same in all locations, due to which currently available PV system is not able to capture sufficient solar radiation to charge the battery in all weather conditions. So, flickering of bulb can be observed during winter season and cloudy days, which decreases the visibility range, cause blurred vision and increases the safety concerns for the remote areas. The key objective of this paper is to design a PV based streetlight using monthly average hourly global solar radiation estimation technique. This method will ensure the accurate design of streetlight according to the location. In this paper NIT Jamshedpur campus is chosen for the prototype model. The value of monthly average solar radiation is calculated by using regression constant in the model suggested by Angstrom Prescott. A standalone PV system with the Boost converter is used for capturing the solar radiation with maximum power-point tracking and storing the generated energy in our designed battery bank. The system designed is according to the calculated average solar radiation for the NIT Jamshedpur campus. The proposed system is simulated using MATLAB/Simulink, and according to the simulated results the performance of system can be observed for all weather conditions.

articleTitle: Simulation of 11kV HDPE Cable Insulation Containing Manufacturing Defects Using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents the study on the performance of High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) as cable insulating materials containing manufacturing defects. In the present work, the effects of voids present in the HDPE insulation due to manufacturing flaws subjected to thermal stress are presented. An 11kV HDPE Cable insulation containing voids is modelled and analyzed in the COMSOL Multiphysics platform. The desirable insulation properties are suitably changed to emulate the effect of thermal aging on the cable insulation. This further enabled carrying out the study related to the electric field distribution in and around the void.

articleTitle: A Novel Circulating Current Control Technique in A Fast Integrated Onboard Charger
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The article introduces a novel three-phase fast, non-isolated integrated onboard charger based on a symmetrical six-phase induction motor (IM). The charger utilizes the drive-train components in the charging process to reduce space, volume, and cost. In the proposed charger circuit, the drive train inverter is used as two parallel connected unity power factor (UPF) rectifiers to form an onboard charger. In parallel-connected UPF rectifiers, there is a problem with circulating currents. To reduce those harmful currents, a novel control technique is proposed in the synchronous reference frame. The interleaved modulation technique is also utilized to reduce ripple current harmonics on both AC and DC sides. The discontinuous pulse width modulation (DPWM) technique is used to reduce switching losses in order to reduce overall charger circuit losses. The DPWM technique results are also compared with the sinusoidal PWM (SPWM) technique. The proposed concept is verified with the help of extensive simulation results.

articleTitle: Crop Yield Prediction Using Linear Regression and Random Forest Modelling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Global warming and climate change profoundly influence life on Earth, significantly impacting ecosystems. Changes in temperature, precipitation patterns, and frost timing affect water availability, crop yields, and the length of growing seasons. These variations may lead to region-specific changes in agricultural practices - enabling the cultivation of new crops in some areas while complicating agriculture in others. This study investigates the impacts of climate change on agricultural yield, focusing on staple cereal crops such as wheat, corn, millet, maize, linseed, olives, and mustard. Leveraging machine learning, this research develops a comparative model to predict crop yields in three key steps. Firstly, weather and crop yield data were collected from various countries over the past two decades. Secondly, data exploration and preprocessing were conducted to prepare datasets for analysis. Lastly, machine learning models were trained using two algorithms: Linear Regression and Random Forest. A comparative analysis of these models' accuracy is presented, with results validated through empirical evaluation.

articleTitle: Design and Demonstration of an IEC 61850-Based Distribution Substation Using Digital Twin Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The digital twin of a substation provides a virtual model that leverages real-time data from Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) to enhance operational efficiency and support data-driven decision-making. With IEC 61850 emerging as the global standard for substation automation, ensuring the interoperability, reliability, and functionality of IEDs within this framework is critical. An IEC 61850 substation employs standardized communication protocols, enabling seamless integration and interoperability among multi-vendor IEDs. Core functionalities include GOOSE (Generic Object-Oriented Substation Event) messaging for rapid, event-driven data exchange, Sampled Values (SV) for accurate analog data transmission, and MMS (Manufacturing Message Specification) for reporting and control functions. To validate and optimize the performance of GOOSE message generation and SV transmission, the IEC 61850 substation model is implemented and tested on the Distributed Test Manager (DTM) platform by Triangle Microworks.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control of Multi-Area Power System using Arctic Puffin Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this study, the authors proposed a realistic model of an interconnected power system to investigate the problem of designing dynamic controllers for load frequency control (LFC). Optimising the PID gain in a two-area network is the goal of the recently released Arctic Puffin Optimisation Algorithm (APO). By setting Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE) as the goal function, the LFC problem is recast as an optimisation problem. Parametric changes to the generator and turbine time constants demonstrate the resilience of the proposed controller. The convergence curve proves that the algorithm is successful, and the time response analysis shows how well the controller is working.

articleTitle: An Efficient Bi-Directional Based Single Phase V2G and G2V Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The increase in electric vehicle mobility has facilitated the development of grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle to grid (V2G)technologies. Electricity can flow both ways between the grid and the batteries of electric vehicles. In this paper a PI based bidirectional control is implemented that all allows power flow can be achieved in both the direction, while maintaining sinusoidal grid currents and maintains unity power factor in the grid. It also improves the electrical system's stability. This leads to improve DC-link voltage management, achieving unity power factor operation, distortionless injection of grid current and smooth transition between V2G and G2V mode. On-board chargers for electric cars (EVs) are developed using (G2V) and (V2G) technology. The power filter implemented herein to reduce the oscillation in the grid current and to mitigates the harmonics in the grid that also improves the performance of the overall system. This work contributes to the growing body of research in EV-grid integration, positioning electric vehicles as a critical component of modern grid infrastructure.

articleTitle: Recent Advancement in Transformer Based Electric Load Forecasting: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Load forecasting (LF) is an integral aspect of power system planning, operations, maintenance, and management. Widespread development of advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) with smart meter adoption has made availability of granular load datasets possible. AI Transformer models have been extensively used for natural language processing (NLP) task. Their capability to learn temporal dependencies from large time series dataset have led to significant research in transformer based time series forecasting. In a decentralized power system with increasing renewable energy sources (RESs) penetration and prosumer participation, LF becomes a complex time series forecasting problem. In recent times, Transformer based model variants have shown to model complex temporal dependencies with greater accuracy. This work surveys pertinent literature to present recent advancement in Transformer based LF models. Simulation studies on benchmarked dataset have shown superior performance of transformer based LF models for varied data granularity and different prediction length as compared to benchmark Deep Learning (DL) models. Model innovations to tackle transformer bottlenecks like space & time complexity are also explored. To conclude, the up-to-date review tries to address open problems and highlights possible future research directions.

articleTitle: Power System Modeling Using Digital Twins for Smart Grid Research Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents suggested approaches for tack-ling digital twin (DT) related issues and simulates the real-life use of a smart grid in advancing DT technology. The forefront concept of DT has caught the attention of many power system research engineers. It has completely transformed the power industry due to recent developments in information and communication technologies (ICT). Power grids currently encounter many challenges, including remote data transmission within the grid and numerous analyses involving real-time data validation. Common smart grid research applications like power system modeling with load flow matching, stability studies in the presence of sub synchronous oscillations, and transmission line fault analysis are verified in real time in this paper. Required power system test systems are modeled in MATLAB Simulink software and validated on the real-time analysis platform Opal-RT OP4510.

articleTitle: A Comparison of AI and Conventional MPPT Technique for Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms driven by artificial intelligence (AI) seek to maximize the power output of renewable energy sources, especially solar panels. In dynamic situations, traditional MPPT methods might not be effective as well. AI algorithms, such as neural networks and reinforcement learning, can quickly adapt to changing environmental conditions (like temperature and sunlight) more effectively than traditional methods. With advancements in computational power, AI can process data in real time, allowing for instantaneous adjustments that traditional methods may not achieve as quickly.

articleTitle: Examination of Signal-to-Noise Ratio in Remote Photoplethysmography Signal Extraction for Video Authenticity Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is a non-invasive technique for assessing physiological signals such as heart rate through facial video recordings. This research investi-gates the impact of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) on selecting rPPG signals from the face region and examines how additional metrics like Power Spectral Density (PSD), Standard Deviation (STD), and Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) contribute to differentiating real and fake videos. The results show that while higher SNR values correlate with more accurate rPPG signal extraction, SNR alone is insufficient for distinguishing authentic and counterfeit videos due to similar SNR distributions. By combining PSD, STD, and MAD, we analyzed key facial regions of interest (ROIs) and implemented in Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier, achieving an accuracy of 98 %. This demonstrates the effectiveness of these metrics in improving accuracy by filtering noise and capturing consistent physiological patterns for detecting deepfakes.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Enhanced Power Quality with Active Power Filters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This article presents hysteresis current controlled <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3}-\boldsymbol{\phi}$</tex> Active Power Filter (APF) employed system aimed enhancing power nature through compensation of harmonics, and demanded reactive power of non-linear load. Shunt AF uses straightforward practice utilizing FFT to determine compensation ref. current. Series AF adopts elementary process on p-q method for compensation ref. voltage. Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC), comprising series & shunt AF connected back-to-back, patterned to d-q-o synchronous rotating ref. axes. Shunt AF neutralizes source's harmonics current and sustain DC link voltage whereas, series AF addresses load harmonics voltage. Traditional filters often underperform in rapidly changing stages, but auto-tuned AF achieve superiority in minimizing harmonics, compensating reactive power & improving pf. Also, paper discusses simulation operation to keep Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in IEEE-519 standards.

articleTitle: Sensing of Biomechanical Properties of Normal and Cancerous Cells Using Micropillar Simulation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Investigation into the biomechanical properties of cells is very critical in understanding their role in disease diagnostics and designing appropriate therapeutic measures. Young's modulus is one such major biomechanical property that gets critically altered in a cancerous cell compared to a healthy one. This alteration can be easily detected by studying the variation in micropillar deflection due to changes in traction force exerted over its surface. In the present study, Young's modulus values of healthy 3T3 fibroblast cells and MCF-7 breast cancer cells were taken from recently published data to obtain the traction force exerted on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> diameter micropillar. This traction force was subsequently used to calculate micropillar deflection using COMSOL Multiphysics software and through mathematical modelling for cell adhesion at three sites over the pillar- at its base, mid-point and tip. The simulation results demonstrated a greater deflection for normal cells, indicating greater traction force due to higher Young's modulus as compared to softer cancerous cells for adhesion at all three regions. Further, simulation results also correlated well with the mathematical models, demonstrating that simple simulation tools may be highly applicable in discriminating a normal cell from a cancerous one.

articleTitle: Application of Pentuple Asymmetrical Microring Resonator as an Optical Filter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this conference paper, the Modeling of a pentuple asymmetrical optical microring resonator (PAOMRR) and its application as an optical filter is based on the Vernier principle. The calculation of the transfer function is done in the Z-domain using Mason's gain formula. Transmittance, normalized group delay, and normalized dispersion of filter are obtained using MATLAB. The proposed model offers an FSR (THz) of 11200, 17300, and 14700. The Q-factors at the respective ports are 1120, 1730, and 1470 respectively. It offers minimal Cross-talk within the 5% band.

articleTitle: Investigation of Modified SEPIC converter with P&O based MPPT for Solar PV
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: A DC-DC converter is necessary in solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to control the fluctuating DC voltage generated by PV cells. An enhanced DC-DC topology that can efficiently raise and stabilize the output voltage while guaranteeing optimal power extraction is the Modified Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC). When used in conjunction with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) approaches, this converter dynamically modifies its output in response to changing environmental conditions. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT algorithm is essential for tracking the maximum power point of the system and reducing oscillations brought on by changes in the surrounding environment. Under changing power demands, the Modified SEPIC Converter with P&O based MPPT enhances system performance, lowers losses, and increases energy efficiency. While extra parts and control methods, such as artificial neural networks, increase the design complexity, ANN based MPPT, the converter achieves more efficiency in real-time applications, providing an excellent balance between flexibility and efficiency. It is perfect for renewable energy systems due to its capacity to function in both step-up and step-down modes.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in PV Grid Integrated System via Machine Learning Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This research presents a study on machine learning algorithms for detecting failures in solar photovoltaic (PV) integrated systems with an exclusive focus on electrical faults. As the use of solar energy increases, maintaining the dependability of PV systems becomes crucial. Using a dataset from a grid-connected PV system, several machine learning algorithms are investigated to find flaws, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, and Random Forest. The issue identification process is automated with the suggested technique, improving system performance, reducing maintenance costs, and increasing efficiency. The results show that machine learning can significantly enhance the sustainability and dependability of solar PV systems.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Combustion in Thermal Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In recent years, the optimization of thermal power plants has become a critical area of research, driven by the urgent need to enhance energy efficiency and reduce emissions. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to optimize the operation of thermal power plants in real-time. RL, a branch of machine learning, offers a promising framework for decision-making in dynamic and uncertain environments, making it well-suited for the complex and nonlinear nature of power plant operations. By integrating RL algorithms with streaming data from sensors and control systems, our proposed methodology enables adaptive and autonomous control of key parameters such as air-fuel ratio and combustion temperature. This approach not only maximizes combustion efficiency but also minimizes emissions of harmful pollutants such as NOx, SOx, and particulate matter. Through simulation studies and real-world experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, paving the way for the next generation of intelligent and sustainable power plant operation. We present a conceptual framework for RL-based control of thermal power plants highlighting potential benefits such as combustion efficiency, improved environmental performance, and enhanced operational flexibility.

articleTitle: Vehicle to Vehicle Conductive Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) conductive charging brings about a new paradigm for energy transfer in electric vehicles (EV), in which one EV can charge another even when the two vehicles are stationary. This method maximizes the usage of EVs and minimizes the need for traditional charging infrastructures while offering a sustainable, flexible solution to the problems posed by modern transportation challenges. The technical feasibility of V2V conductive charging systems is discussed in terms of system design simplicity, cross-vehicle compatibility, and integrated safety measures. Major advantages of this technology include increased vehicle range, reduced downtime of charging, and increased energy delivery to EVs. The present study lays the basis for transforming electric mobility and facilitating more efficient transportation through the implementation of V2V charging systems by addressing the aforementioned

articleTitle: Condition Assessment of Dielectric Liquid Used in Large Power Equipment Using Time-Varying Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents a non-invasive approach for assessing the condition of dielectric liquids, particularly mineral oils, used in power transformers by employing a Time-Varying Model (TVM) to analyze polarization current profiles. Ageing in dielectric liquids can compromise transformer reliability. Hence, effective monitoring is essential. In this study, mineral oil samples are subjected to accelerated ageing, with polarization current measurements analyzed via TVM. Performance parameters, including conductivity, dissipation factor, and relative permittivity, are evaluated using variance analysis to reveal more distinct ageing trends compared to traditional standard deviation methods. Findings suggest that variance analysis provides a more accurate depiction of oil degradation, supporting condition-based maintenance and reducing transformer failure risks.

articleTitle: Power Sharing Scheme for PV-Battery Type MG with Inclusion of Communication Link Failure
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Increasing the contribution of renewable energy sources (RESs) is a vital contribution in mitigating the adverse effects of using fossils. Among various RESs, solar photovoltaic (PV) is most preferred one having maximum adoption due to the abundance of solar insolation on Earth. Because solar power output is variable, battery storage is often combined with PV to create a PV-battery system within a microgrid (MG). It is essential to ensure proper power distribution among the multiple units, especially under faulty conditions or component failures. The centralized secondary controller provides accurate power sharing among parallel PV-battery units via the low-bandwidth communication channels. However, system efficiency is highly affected when the communication channel is unavailable. Thus, the decentralized secondary control (DSC) algorithm needs updating to maintain a stable operation for individual units and the MG as a whole during communication outages. Additionally, the microgrid may form multiple separate networks or nano-grids due to scheduled maintenance or faults. To ensure stability and reliability within these isolated networks, the centralized decentralized secondary controller (CDSC) algorithm requires enhancements for effective power sharing among PV-battery units in the newly created networks. The PSCAD/EMTDC tool is utilized to simulate the modified EU distribution network for assessing the performance of this improved control scheme and results suggests some good outcomes.

articleTitle: Improvement of Frequency Stability in Airport Microgrids by Nonlinear Generation Control
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper analyses a remote airport microgrid, incorporating autonomous renewable energy sources (RES) like Archimedes Wave Energy Conversion, Wind Turbine Generator, Solar Tower, and Photovoltaic Energy (PV). Besides, it includes regulated generating units, namely, micro-turbine power generators, biogas turbine generators, and biodiesel generators. The energy storage systems mainly involve electric vehicles, ultracapacitors, and battery energy storage systems. With respect to the microgrid load frequency control and grid stability, a fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative controller is used. The mentioned above optimization techniques are supposed to be used to obtain the controllers' parameters: Chimp Optimization Algorithm, Artificial Rabbit Optimization, and Heap-Based Optimization. It performs better than ARO and CHOA, and thus it shows superior frequency stabilization, less overshot, and a faster settling time as indicated by simulation data. Thus, optimizing the control strategy of a microgrid will provide a strong, scalable approach toward sustainability, flexibility, and reliability for an airport microgrid under various load scenarios.

articleTitle: Improving Frequency Regulation in Interconnected Islanded Microgrids Through Nonlinear Control and Cogeneration Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper studies frequency control and area control error (ACE) minimization in interconnected marine and airport microgrids utilizing various conventional and renewable energy sources (RESs), dynamic loads, and energy storage systems. The management of load demand balancing and frequency regulation in these systems is achieved through the implementation of a fractional order PID controller (FOPID). Various optimization techniques, such as Mountain Gazelle Optimization (MGO), Swaram Optimization, Coati Optimization Algorithm, and Artificial Electric Field Algorithm, are used to fine-tune the parameters of the FOPID controller. The optimized FOPID controller MGO outperforms other algorithms by accurately matching generation and demand under different load conditions, reducing ACE, and ensuring robust frequency requirements. Despite the variability of RESs, the proposed design significantly improves the stability and reliability of isolated and interconnected microgrids. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the MGO algorithm in complex microgrid environments and help improve system performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Satin Bowerbird Optimized Automatic Generation Control with Cyber Resilient Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The communication infrastructure of the modern power systems helps to improve the benefits of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) but vulnerable to cyber threats. Therefore, this paper suggests AGC of interconnected power system with cyber resilient mechanism to discriminate the cyber-attacks from the normal load perturbations and to initiate the control operation of the plants. For AGC, proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers are used in the secondary control loops of interconnected areas and the gains of the controllers are optimized with satin bowerbird optimizer (SBO) using integral square error as fitness function. Prior to control action, attack detection mechanism is used with the help of multiple linear regression to detect the cyber-attacks from the normal load variations. The effectiveness of the scheme is tested on both load disturbances and false data injections to show its discrimination ability and improvements in the AGC response of the power system.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Non Superconducting Fault Current Limiter for Low Voltage Ride-Through for Protection of DFIG Wind Generator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Wind energy is getting considerable attention due to its efficiency and reliability. However, the effectiveness relies on the environmental condition, as it depends on the wind speed. The incorporation of energy storage reduces its intermittency effect. Various types of wind generators are available, where doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is an important generator due to its rigid construction. The direct coupling of the stator with the grid results a high sensitivity in the system. The fault occurrence affects the stator terminal and hence the overall system. To safeguard the DFIG system an adaptive non super conducting fault current limiter (ANSFCL) is designed in this paper. To gauge its efficacy it is developed under various scenarios. The fault consequences are evaluated under various uncertainties conditions which is useful under severe fault condition. The simulation is being carried out using MATLAB Simulink based environment.

Author Keywords: adaptive non super conducting fault current limiter (ANSFCL)

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Grid-Following and Grid-Forming Control Techniques Used in Inverter-based Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The future framework for energy systems is expected to be a power grid that is largely powered by renewable energy sources (RESs). The commonly utilized grid-following (GFL) control method for grid-connected converters has difficulties in this configuration, including decreased stability and restricted grid support capabilities. Grid-forming (GFM) control techniques have recently been devised to improve these grid-tied converters' dynamic performance and stability. Among the different types of GFM techniques, scientists widely accept the droop control technique because it is simple to design, easy to scale, and operates as a decentralized control method, making it less reliant on communication links and, therefore, more reliable. Thus, the study presents a comprehensive review of the latest advancements in droop control techniques.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring of DC Microgrids of Solar Farms Using an MQTT-Based IIoT Device with Node-RedIntegration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a real-time monitoring system for DC microgrids in solar farms using an MQTT-based IIoT device integrated with Node-RED. The system incorporates voltage and current sensors connected to solar panels, with an ESP32 microcontroller reading data from the sensors to calculate power output. This data is transmitted to a Raspberry Pi server via a WiFi network, utilizing the MQTT protocol for efficient and reliable communication. Node-RED manages and visualizes the data flow, providing a user-friendly interface through its dashboard for monitoring real-time voltage, current, and power readings. This integration of IIoT devices with Node-RED streamlines data collection, processing, and visualization, enhancing solar farms' overall monitoring and control. The proposed system's scalability allows for the seamless addition of new sensors and microgrids without substantial modifications, addressing the need for flexible expansion in large-scale solar farms. Detailed flow diagrams and performance evaluations are included to demonstrate the system's effectiveness and reliability in real-time applications. Compared to existing monitoring solutions, this system offers lower costs, higher scalability, and enhanced real-time data processing capabilities, making it suitable for deployment in various renewable energy environments.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Ring Resonator Embedded with High Contrast Optical Bragg Grating in Z-Domain for Optical Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The integration of ring resonators with Bragg gratings have emerged as promising optical filters because of their compact size and good spectral selectivity. A comprehensive mathematical modeling and analysis of such a system is presented to precisely capture the resonance characteristics and transmission spectra of the system using delay-line signal processing and Z-domain analysis, followed by a discussion on related potential application as well as challenges in modern optical systems. The simulation results indicate improved filtering precision and sharp resonance peaks, indicating excellent performance.

articleTitle: Unveiling Role of Size, Wet Layer Thickness, and Interface Potential Barrier on the Confinement Effect of the Conical, Cylindrical and Spherical Quantum Dots
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This research work presents an impact on the energy states and probability density of finding electrons due to the confinement of different size parameters such as quantum dot (QD) radius, QD height, wetting layer (WL) thickness, and even potential barrier for coupled conical shape QD with WL system. For its reliable comparison, another two QDs proposed namely cylindrical and spherical QD, coupled with WL. These nanostructures are modeled with InAs and GaAs material. The InAs is considered to form QDs with WL on the GaAs substrate. We have computed the eigen energies corresponding to the carrier confined in three-dimensional QDs with a WL (quantum well) coupled system. The problems are formulated with effective mass approximation, Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions; and 1-band Schrodinger wave equation in partial differential equation are solved in coefficient form. The non-uniform finite element methodology discretized the Schrodinger wave equation. To find different state's eigenvalues the ARPCAK solver has been implemented. These methodologies are implemented on all proposed structures in this work for fair comparison. We observed that along with size confinement of QDs and WL, the potential barrier and different shapes also play crucial roles in modeling highly optimized QDs. From result analysis overall we found that the probability of finding e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>is relatively large in CO-QD and eigen value are higher for SP-QD. The investigation revealed that the QDs have optimum radius for the given height and vice versa for the minimum bandgap and eventually the optimum optical efficiency. We also found that these optimized QDs have promising features that make them potentially usable in devices for quantum hardware in quantum computing for information processing.

articleTitle: Target Classification in Radar Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In radar systems, precise target classification is essential for effective situational awareness. We developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based approach to classify radar targets using their signal characteristics automatically. Compared to traditional methods, our solution demonstrates higher accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency while addressing challenges like data labelling, interpretability, and signal variability. The results highlight the potential of deep learning to transform radar systems, enhancing applications in military surveillance and autonomous navigation. This work marks a significant step toward seamlessly integrating deep learning with radar technologies.

articleTitle: PV Array Fault Detection and Location Estimation Using Ensemble Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Currently, large-scale grid connected solar power plants are being installed in MW range for electricity generation. The PV arrays of these large-scale solar power plants are exposed to different electrical faults. The misdetection of faults can create problems in effective operation of solar power plant and can also lead to fire hazards. The magnitude of fault current depends on the irradiance level as well as number of modules getting affected. Consequently, the change in the magnitude of fault currents especially during high impedance ground faults and low mismatch faults is insignificant. The fixed fuse rating of conventional protection schemes like overcurrent protection devices and ground fault detection interrupters have limitations in detection of such crucial faults. In this paper, an ensemble learning model-based technique is used for detection of faults and faulted strings in PV arrays using string current and array voltage simulated through MATLAB/Simulink. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated and demonstrated through simulated results.

articleTitle: Insulator Fault Detection in Aerial Images Using YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Insulator faults are a severe threat to the safety and stability of power transmission lines. Accurate and fast detection of these faults is paramount for preventive maintenance and grid reliability. This paper explores the application of You Only Look Once version 9 (YOLOv9), a state-of-the-art deep learning object detection model, for insulation fault detection in power line imagery. The effectiveness of YOLOv9 in identifying healthy insulators from those exhibiting various fault types is investigated. The paper details the training process, including data preparation, model configuration, and optimization techniques. Standard metrics like mean average precision (mAP) are used to analyze the performance of the YOLOv9 mode and the confusion matrix is used to identify potential areas for improvement. The findings of this research contribute to the development of automated and efficient insulation fault detection systems, enhancing power grid maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Toe-In Braking in Longitudinal Motion for 4WIS4WID EV
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents toe-in braking in the longitudinal motion of a four-wheel independent steering four-wheel independent drive (4WIS4WID) electric vehicle (EV) in its heading direction. The steering function in these EVs allows achieving toe-in braking without any significant modification of the hardware. It uses an established mathematical model of 4WIS4WID EV and slightly modifies an existing path-tracking control scheme to achieve toe-in braking. The toe-in algorithm uses a feed-forward scheme with two serial components: The first helps specify the required deceleration rate, while the second helps compute the toe-in angle that helps meet this deceleration rate. Analysis shows effect of varying toe-in angle on forces and slips during braking, and on stopping time. Analysis for input-to-state stability of the said modified scheme helps develop a constraint on allowable toe-in angles. It simulates two situations with toe-in braking. The first involves velocity tracking in an open-loop configuration, while the second involves path tracking using a closed-loop configuration. Simulation results agree with the above analysis.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Modified Leaky LMS Based Control Scheme for Single-Stage and Dual-Stage Three-Phase Grid-Tied PV System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) based distributed generation (DG) helps meeting continuously increasing power demand. Effective control of PV-based DG becomes crucial for its integration into the power network. This paper presents a Modified Leaky Least Mean Square (MLLMS) algorithm based control scheme for SSGPV and DSGPV three-phase grid-tied PV system. The DSGPV system consists of a PV array, a dc-dc boost converter controlled using Incremental Conductance (InC) technique for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation and three-phase DG for dc to ac conversion, which is integrated with the utility grid. In a SSGPV system, DG is controlled for MPPT operation as well as power exchange with the grid and load. The presented grid-tied DG employs MLLMS based control scheme to generate the reference grid currents. Simulation analysis of the given SSGPV and DSGPV DG performance is carried out using MATLAB. The PV based DG effectively exchanges power with the grid as well as feeds to the load. It balances grid currents even in case of unbalanced load condition. The transient response of the DG is analysed for irradiation change and load unbalanced condition. Simulation results depict satisfactory steady-state as well as transient response of grid-tied PV based DG.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fractional-order PI-PD Controller Design with Indirect Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this article, a Hybrid controller structure with fractional order Proportional Integral (PI) and Integer order Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller is proposed (FOPI-PD) for stable and unstable first-order processes. The proposed controller structure consists of a Feed-forward fractional order PI controller and Feedback integer order PD controller. The Proportional Derivative controller in feedback gives a better regulatory response as compared to the Feed-forward PD controller; and the fractional-order PI Controller in feed-forward helps to achieve the better Servo response. Analytical tuning rules are proposed for the FOPI-PD controller with the help of Gain and Phase Margin analysis. After that, the proposed controller is further fine-tuned with the Fractional Indirect Design approach-2 to mitigate the mathematical approximation errors and improve the performance of the proposed controller. Additionally, it is shown that the robustness of the FOPI-PD controller can be adjusted with a single variable in a given range. The proposed controller is validated with the help of the MATLAB simulation examples on the First-order Stable and Unstable processes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of IoT-Based Automatic Power Factor Correction Relay Using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper illustrates the design and implementation of an IOT -based automatic power factor correction (APFC) relay using Raspberry Pi in electrical power distribution systems. Power quality is crucial across numerous non-linear consumers in power distribution systems (PDS). One of the essential factors determining the power quality is the power factor. In PDS, the power factor can deteriorate due to factors such as AC motors, water pumps, welding instruments, transformers, voltage regulators, arcs & induction heaters, choke wires, neon signs, etc. Besides, all industries require consistent power quality for many applications daily. High-quality electricity improves productivity, eliminates technical issues, and lowers energy costs. A poor power factor for the PDS causes huge amounts of line losses, low voltage problems, and thermal problems in switchgear. Therefore, automatic power factor improvement plays a significant role in reducing electricity consumption and ensuring more efficient system operation. To solve this problem, in this paper, the design and simulation of a single-phase APFC with IOT utilizing a Raspberry Pi Pico (W) are described. Here, CT and PT measure current and voltage; an XOR gate measures the angle between voltage and current. A suitable algorithm is coded for the Raspberry PI to obtain the desired power factor (0.99 to 0.98), and according to IEC 61921:2017, calculated capacitor banks (04 stages) are used. Besides, IOT is interfaced through ThingSpeak to show the real-time data of an APFC relay using the internet from anywhere to monitor it properly. Furthermore, the theoretical and simulated results are validated using 1000-watt prototype inductive loads (induction motor).

articleTitle: Reactive Power Compensation in Hybrid Power System using African Vulture Optimized Statcom Tilt Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Reactive power imbalance in hybrid power systems is due to the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources and different load disturbances. Dynamic voltage stability and reactive power compensation (RPC) are achieved by the implementation of flexible AC transmission system (FACTs) devices. This paper explores the enhancement of RPC and voltage stability in a standalone wind diesel hybrid power system (SWDHPS) through the utilization of a novel African Vulture optimized STATCOM-integral minus tilit derivative with filter coefficient controller (STATCOM-I-TDN). The performance of the proposed controller is compared with traditional controllers. Analysis revealed that the dynamic voltage response of the proposed controller outperformed others.

Author Keywords: Standalone wind diesel hybrid power system (SWDHPS)

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Sensorless Control of Flyback Converter for Cell Balancing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: A conventional control system with an active clamp flyback converter uses a feedforward method that involves feeding the input to a mathematical model beforehand to adjust the duty cycle accordingly. The feedforward method uses a mathematical model that involves a lot of calculations to obtain an efficiency alike feedback system. Integrating a neural network trained with a feedback system data output can be used as a replacement for the mathematical model to have performance as par with the feedback system. Sensors are used to measure the voltages for the feedback circuit to work. This work investigates the potential of utilizing a neural network to enable sensorless operation within a feedforward control system to regulate the voltage input to the cell balancina system.

articleTitle: Satellite Image Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Image classification is crucial in remote sensing, image analysis, and pattern recognition. Object detection and classification in satellite images are crucial for applications like marine monitoring, land-use planning, ecological research, and military operations. Satellite images provide valuable spatial and temporal data, helping address real-world challenges. However, issues like data quality, availability, and distribution complicate image analysis. Deep learning (DL) algorithms have become popular for their effectiveness in classifying satellite images, sup-porting tasks such as disaster management, land-use planning, and natural resource management. This study proposed a CNN model with batch normalization for satellite image classification. The dataset includes images categorized into cloudy regions, deserts, water bodies, and green spaces. CNN excels at extracting features like edges and textures, while Batch Normalization (BN) stabilizes training by normalizing inputs and reducing covariate shifts. Together, CNN and BN improve the efficiency and accuracy of the model. The proposed model successfully classifies satellite images, outperforming existing methods with an overall accuracy of 91%, demonstrating its superior remote sensing imaae analysis capability.

articleTitle: Smart Load Shedding Designed for Unintentional Islanding of Steel Plants with Captive Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Iron and steel plants are bulk consumers of power and although, depend on the utility/grid for their operation and production, a captive power and blowing station with an inhouse power generation takes care of the emergency loads of the plant, in case of unintentional islanding. While safe Islanding would protect the generators and other ‘hot’ equipment, smart load shedding with judicious categorization of the loads would help continue the coke and hot metal production in the steel plant. This paper develops an Islanding and Load shedding philosophy for steel plants with the concept of matching of the generated power with the connected loads using a dynamic automation model. By ensuring power to the energy sources namely coke oven and Blast furnace continue to operate with the available power, the production of coke and hot metal shall also remain uninterrupted. The paper also presents a case study illustrating the implementation of the scheme beginning with categorizing the essential processes, prioritizing the loads and preserving the Island's power distribution stability. As these units are spaced over a large geographical area, the interplant electrical SCADA architecture is employed as a backbone for communication of the load shedding system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of High Resistance Grounding in Medium Voltage Marine Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Grounding schemes play a significant role in maintaining the safety and operational efficiency onboard ships. The widely preferred grounding scheme is the floating neutral system due to the advantage of continual operation despite a fault in any of the phases. However, the transient voltages during the fault may result in multi-phase faults and eventually damage the complete system. The High Resistance Grounding (HRG) scheme resolves this problem while retaining all the benefits of an ungrounded system. The complexity in implementing the HRG scheme lies in choosing a resistor whose magnitude is less than the charging capacitance of the system. As per IEEE 45.4 −2018, the HRG scheme is recommended for LV systems only. To extend the benefits of HRG to MV systems, a comprehensive analysis with real-time data is necessary. In this paper, the performance of the HRG system for MV ship systems is evaluated, considering the specific challenges and design considerations unique to MV systems. The results of the HRG system are found satisfactory as the transients are not reflected when a high impedance fault is created.

articleTitle: An Analogous Virtual Synchronous Machine-Based Virtual Inertia Control Strategy for Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Modern power system (PS) demands the penetration of various types of renewable energy sources (RESs) through power electronic devices into the grid. But the main disadvantage of this RES penetration includes different types of stability problems like system-frequency oscillation, damping, moment of inertia etc. To mitigate this issue, a Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy is used that takes the help of the rotor behaviour of the traditional synchronous generator (SG). It is observed from the literature that a synchronous generator provides both voltage(V) and frequency(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>) support in PS. With the help of this V, f support, VSG can able to remove the different detrimental problems of the penetration of RESs in PS as mentioned previously. In this paper, the frequency of the inverter is found by using the swing equation of the SG and from this frequency of the inverter, the rotor angle is obtained. The entire system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink® environment. It is observed from simulation results that during the transient condition, the rotor angle lies between 0° to 15°. So, the system is found to be stable irrespective of different load conditions.

articleTitle: Power Sharing in Multiple PV-Battery Based MG System by Considering Component Isolation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Increasing renewable energy resources contribution helps to reduce the ill effects of use of fossil fuels. Solar PV have highest percentage of use amongst all renewable as the solar insolation is available on earth in plentiful. Due to variability of power output, storage battery are also used along with PV resulting in PV-battery system within a microgrid (MG) system. Proper power sharing under failure of components under any faulty condition must be taken into account. The centralized secondary controller offers an accurate power sharing with the parallel attached PVB terminals through the low bandwidth communication channel/network. However, the performance of the system is significantly affected during the non-availability of the communication network. Therefore, the DSC algorithm needs to be updated to offer the stable operation of individual unit and overall microgrid for the duration in which the communication network is unavailable. Further, the isolation of the microgrid component(s) because of scheduled maintenance or the fault results in multiple separate networks/parts of the microgrid. Hence, the CDSC algorithm need to be upgraded to offer the stable and reliable operation of the newly formed networks/parts or nano-grids. Moreover, it offers proper power sharing among the available PVB units within the newly formed networks.
