The PSCAD/EMTDC tool is used to develop the simulation model of the modified EU distribution network for evaluating the system performance of the developed control scheme.

articleTitle: Synchrophasor Measurement Using the Perfectly Flat-Top FIR Filter for M-Class PMU
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Synchrophasor measurement, an emerging technology, plays a crucial role in the real-time monitoring and control of smart grid applications. It allows for the effective supervision and control of real-time power system parameters under dynamic conditions. The phasor estimation approach is the most crucial factor in determining the accuracy of the synchrophasor measurement. This paper presents the phasor estimation using the finite impulse response (FIR) filter designed by the perfectly flat-top window. Furthermore, it provides a comprehensive performance evaluation under the steady-state, dynamic-state compliance tests, noise, and several harmonics distortions as IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1:2018 recommended. The IEC/IEEE standard signal processing model with Hamming window functions also compares performance. The evaluation of phasor estimation, frequency measurement, and rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) measurement was conducted using the total vector error (TVE), frequency error (FE), and ROCOF error (RFE), respectively. The analysis of the results shows that the performance of phasor estimation by the FIR filter created with the perfectly flat-top window is more accurate than the existing work done at a lower sampling rate. The design and performance analysis of the phasor estimation are performed on the MAT LAB platform.

articleTitle: Design and Assessment of DC-DC Interleaved Flyback Stage for Module-Integrated PV Microinverters
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Microinverters are typically integrated with individual solar photovoltaic (PV) modules to enhance system performance. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an interleaved flyback DC-DC converter for microinverters in a methodical approach. The flyback converter is selected for its advantages, including a reduced component count and a simplified architecture. Additionally, it provides electrical isolation, meeting grid code requirements, and offers high voltage gain, making it suitable for a wide range of input voltages. The time-interleaved operation of the DC-DC flyback stage, utilizing multiple parallel switching phases, effectively reduces ripple current, minimizes component stress, and improves power density. An active clamp circuit is incorporated to recover leakage energy. The operational principles, including all modes of operation, are thoroughly explained. The complete design is presented with relevant mathematical formulations and validated through software simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Adaptive Filtering Algorithm Controlled STATCOM for LVRT Capability Enhancement of DFIG
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This work focuses on enhancing transient stability or low voltage ride-through (LVRT) in a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) by dynamically tuning all the PI controllers of the STATCOM using a novel approach. The hybrid enhanced block sphere Bayesian’ algorithm (EBSBA) and ‘least mean square root of exponential’ (LMSRE) algorithms (EBSBA- LMSRE) is proposed as a solution, offering key advantages such as high convergence speed, low computational complexity, and a straightforward design. The main goal of this work is to address voltage fluctuations and restore stable conditions in the DFIG. In this work, the cascaded structure-based proportional integral (PI) controllers are implemented on the voltage source converter (VSC) of the static synchronous compensator (STATCOM). During the transient, the gain of the PI controllers is automatically adjusted by the proposed hybrid EBSBA-LMSRE algorithm. The EBSBA-LMSRE-PI controlled STATCOM demonstrates superior response and damping compared to the LMSRE-PI and EBESBA-PI controllers, especially under normal and abnormal grid disturbances.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transmission Using Additively Manufactured Ferrite Pad
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is a promising technology for various purposes, but efficiency remains a key challenge. This research investigates using additively manufactured ferrite pads to enhance wireless power transmission efficiency. By utilizing manganese-zinc ferrite cores with precise 3D-printed geometries, the study aims to improve magnetic flux coupling and reduce energy losses. Using ANSYS Maxwell simulations and experimental setups with AWG 40 Litz wire coils, the research explored how ferrite materials impact power transfer performance. The findings demonstrate the significant improvements: simulations achieved a transfer efficiency of 89% while the experimental data showed output results increasing from 26.27 mV to 40.46 mV when using a ferrite pad. The study addresses critical WPT challenges such as coil misalignment, distance variations, and power density, offering insights into developing more efficient wireless charging solutions and other applications.

articleTitle: Wireless Solar-Powered Solution for Electric Vehicle Charging and Energy Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated solar wireless EV charging system, emphasizing AI -driven optimization for energy management. The system integrates solar panels, wireless charging modules, and a Gradient Boosting Regression model, achieving an R-squared value of 0.987 for EV range prediction using a dataset of 400 EV metrics. Prototype testing validates the model by correlating solar power variability with EV per-formance predictions. The system demonstrates 80 % wireless charging efficiency and highlights sustainable, efficient charging solutions. This study showcases the potential of combining re-newable energy and AI to optimize EV charging infrastructures, advancing sustainability and addressing energy management challenges.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Autonomous Fire Mitigating Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Fire incidents in hazardous or remote areas require quick response to prevent extensive damage. This paper presents an IoT -based autonomous firefighting robot designed to detect fire hazards and provide real-time location data for emergency responders. The system is built using an Arduino micro controller and integrates GPS technology for precise tracking. This approach provides a cost-effective, efficient solution for early fire detection and response, with potential applications in environments requiring continuous monitoring.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Power Load Prediction using LSTM in a Smart Grid Scenario for Household Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The smart grid fuses modern technology with traditional infrastructure to enhance efficiency and sustainability. Accurate Load Forecasting (LF) is crucial for ensuring reliability and rising electricity demand, while integration of machine learning transforms energy and grid management. In this research real-time consumption of historical power load data from house hold smart meters is used. The aim of this paper is to choose the best machine learning algorithm with good accuracy which helps to predict the future power load and assess the load forecasts with low Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and high R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score. Our research involved the implementation of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms using load forecasting. This paper results the effectiveness and efficiency of ML algorithms in predicting future power loads, with LSTM demonstrating low RMSE, MAPE, of 1.40 and 0.03(%) and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score of 0.909 respectively. Overall, the integration of ML algorithms in load forecasting for smart grids shows great potential for enhancing efficiency and reliability in energy management.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Level SVPWM Scheme for High Power Induction Motor Drive Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-level inverter (MLI) topology for an OEWIM (Open-End Winding Induction Motor) drive is proposed. In this topology, one end of OEWIM is fed by a FC based hybrid 5-level inverter and other end is connected to a symmetrical 5-level inverter. The hybrid 5-level inverter is achieved by cascading a 3-level flying capacitor inverter with capacitor fed H-bridge. The symmetrical 5-level inverter is obtained by cascade connection of four 2-level inverters with equal DC-link voltages. The combined effect of 5-level hybrid and 5-level symmetrical inverters generate 25 distinct levels in the phase voltage. In this proposed topology, a total of 3,43,000 space phasor combinations are accessible; hence using switching redundancies, the capacitor voltages can be maintained at desired levels. The proposed topology requires only 48 switching devices, as compared to conventional topologies that require 144 switches and fully eliminates the requirement of clamping diodes, which are required in NPC inverter. It, also, requires only 6 capacitors unlike to 828 capacitors required in 25-level FC inverter and 5 DC power supply sources as compared to 25-level CHB inverter that require 36 DC power supply sources. Hardware-in-loop (HIL) validation of simulation results is carried out to evaluate the performance of the proposed inverter and results are presented.

articleTitle: Quantifying Solar Cell Power Output in the Lab: A MATLAB-Based Approach with Artificial Illumination
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a detailed methodology for measuring the power output of solar cells. It utilizes an analytical and simulation-based approach to evaluate the effectiveness of outdoor solar cells in natural sunlight against their performance in an indoor laboratory setting using artificial illumination. The study endeavors to establish a dependable and reproducible framework for assessing the effectiveness of photovoltaic systems, which is essential for enhancing the efficiency of photovoltaic technologies. MATLAB/ Simulink platform is used to simulate solar cell behavior under different solar irradiation and light intensities, allowing precise control over the variables in our experiments. Outdoor measurements capture performance in real-world scenarios, while indoor setups provide controlled testing environments. The results presented in our study clearly illustrate the differences in power output observed in different settings, emphasizing the significant impact that the characteristics of the light source have on the efficiency of solar cells. By employing a dual-approach comparison, a comprehensive understanding of solar cell behavior is achieved, leading to the development of more effective testing protocols and advancements in photovoltaic designs. The accuracy and flexibility of the MATLAB model highlight its usefulness in solar energy research, making it a valuable tool for both academic studies and industry applications. The findings make a valuable contribution to the progress of solar technology, as they successfully connect the results obtained in controlled laboratory settings with the actual performance of solar systems in real-world conditions.

articleTitle: From Conveyor Belts to Crushers: A Review on Radial and Axial Flux Induction Motor Advances and Applications in Industrial Mining Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper typically reviews the classification, design, and applications of induction motors (IMs), focusing on radial flux induction motors (RFIMs) and axial flux induction motors (AFIMs), particularly in the mining sector. RFIMs, known for their robustness and cost-effectiveness, are preferred for equipment such as conveyors, pumps, and ventilation systems. Recent advancements include enhanced topologies and techniques to improve performance and reliability. AFIMs, with their compact design and high torque capabilities, offer advantages in space-constrained applications. Innovations like multi-stator/multi-rotor configurations and optimized control strategies enable these motors to excel in harsh environments. The document also addresses inrush current mitigation techniques, including adjustable frequency drives, for harsh mining environments. Emphasizing durability, reliability, and energy efficiency, these developments ensure that induction motors meet the rigorous demands of industrial and mining environments.

articleTitle: Reviews on PQ Improvement of RES Integrated Distribution Network by Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Day by day increment in electrical energy increases the need for renewable energy sources along with conventional fossil fuel-based energy. Therefore, in so many cases individuals are preparing their own RES harvesting equipment as small-scale projects. But in this approach, the effectiveness is not that significant for the entire population. That is why in recent days the implementation of RES-based generation units is becoming very common in the main distribution network so that the demand can be fulfilled as well as the environmental sustainability can be maintained. At the same time, such types of implementations have the worst effects on the PQ in terms of reactive power increment and the presence of harmonics. Therefore, it is becoming essential to compensate for those uncertainties otherwise the equipment that will be connected to the distribution network will not work properly. The variation of loads, variation in the generation due to sunlight irradiance change, wind speed changes the electrical quantities like current, voltage, and frequency are becoming distorted, these are the things named as PQ indices. Here in this paper, we are researching the successful implementation of RES generating stations and power injection to the mainline without creating any disturbance. For that, the usage of a shunt active power filter plays an important role. Using shunt active power filters and different controlling strategies the line power qualities are now improved a lot. Based on this concept all the technicality and research data are presented in this paper for better understanding.

articleTitle: Intelligent Energy Management with ANFIS Based Strategy for Enhancing Battery Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) has enhanced their integration into modern power systems, but their inherent intermittency presents significant challenges. To address these fluctuations, Energy Storage Systems (ESS) are increasingly employed; however, managing the complex interactions between multiple RES, flexible loads, and ESS poses a substantial challenge for traditional rule-based control systems. This study evaluates the performance of the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) in optimizing battery management, comparing it to conventional Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC). An ANFIS controller was designed to manage battery states-specifically charging, discharging, and floating—by leveraging critical input variables such as Battery State of Charge (BSoC), Power Demand (PD), and Generated Power (Pgen). The model exhibited remarkable adaptability through the iterative optimization of its membership functions and rules, in contrast to the static framework of traditional Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC). The obtained simulation outcomes demonstrate that ANFIS substantially outperforms FLC across essential performance in different metrics. The overall findings underscore the considerable potential of ANFIS in advancing adaptive control methodologies within energy systems, ultimately facilitating more efficient management of energy resources.

articleTitle: Effective Control of Speed and Regenerative Braking in Electric Vehicles Utilizing Fractional Order PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In the automotive industry, a significant application of the Proportional Integral (PI) controller is in electric motors, specifically Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motors used in Electric Vehicles (EVs). The accuracy of speed regulation in BLDC motors, acclaimed for their effectiveness and dependability, is crucial for enhancing vehicle performance and ensuring energy efficiency. On the other hand, regenerative braking is also important for energy recovery during vehicle navigation. In this paper, fractional order PI controller (FOPI) is implemented for smooth and precise control of speed and energy recovery during regenerative braking. Conventional Ziegler-Nichols method is used to tune the gains of the controller and for better controlling <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> value for fractional order PI is predicted using trial and error method over extensive simulations on Simulink environment. The simulation results show accurate control of speed by variation of desired speed from 1500 rpm to 2800 rpm with fast transient response and without any delay. Energy recovery has been implemented through regenerative braking and show the battery charging and reverse flow of current during deceleration and applied braking in the EV.

articleTitle: Fuzzy PSO Algorithm for Optimal DG Integration in a Practical Indian Distribution Network Using Logic OR-Based Forward Backward Load Flow
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of distributed generation (DG) resources has become more prevalent due to their positive influence on electrical systems. On the other hand, incorrect DG unit placement and sizing can increase losses and negatively impact voltage stability. Effective methods for integrating DG into Distribution Networks (DN) are crucial for reducing these difficulties. In DNs with high resistance-to-reactance (R/X) ratios, conventional Newton Raphson Load Flow (NR-LF) methods often face difficulties because of the singularity of the Jacobian matrix. To overcome this, a Logic OR-Based Forward Backward Load Flow (FB-LF) method, utilizing simplified matrix computations, is proposed for load flow analysis. The multi-objective optimization problem is addressed using a Fuzzy based Mixed Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (MD-PSO) algorithm, enhanced by the Modified Fuzzy max-min principle. A real-world 28-bus distribution network with a range of load scenarios is used to validate the methodology. Additionally, the results are compared with those obtained from the standard 69-bus distribution network. The suggested technique's ability to reduce convergence time and computational complexity is demonstrated by the results, which also examine power losses and voltage profiles under various loading scenarios.

Author Keywords: DG placement for different load types

articleTitle: Evaluation of Uncertainty and Stochastic Modelling of Renewable Energy Sources in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The power system confronts considerable issues owing to the high fluctuation and unpredictability coming from the increasing expansion of wind energy, photovoltaic (PV) systems, and electric vehicle (EV) charging requirements. Constant uncertainty in energy systems challenges the characterisation of deterministic characteristics inside power networks. This underlines the necessity of making informed judgments from both management and operational viewpoints. This chapter presents a comprehensive introduction of numerous uncertainty models used in power system planning and operation, including those for load demand, wind energy, PV energy, PEVs, electricity pricing, and load growth. The purpose is to give a complete framework for controlling uncertainty in power systems. By synthesizing these models, the chapter tries to incorporate uncertainty management into the planning and operation phases, allowing the assessment of choices, cost estimate, revenue projection, and the reduction of possible hazards.

articleTitle: Dynamic Load Scheduling Optimization Utilizing the Rao Algorithm for Improved System Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper explores the optimal scheduling of conventional generating units for two dynamic test systems, and enhances the systems performance. The Rao algorithmic approach, a parameter-free population-based optimization method, is utilized to improve the solutions through cooperative interactions on the basis of the best and worst candidate solutions in each iteration. Practical factors, such as ramp-rate limits, valve point effects and transmission loss, were incorporated to reflect real-world operational challenges. The Rao algorithm achieved high-quality solutions in terms of generation cost and reduced pollutant emission. These results highlight the effectiveness of the algorithm in solving complex nonlinear optimization problems and improving the efficiency of dynamic load scheduling.

articleTitle: A Design of Hybrid Model and Bayesian Neural Networks for Smart Grid Stability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The latest evolution in power systems, is ‘smart grids'that offers real time monitoring, control features as well as effective management of renewable energy sources. Nonetheless, with the increase in the system complexity, the chances for insta- bility also increase and thus it is crucial to forecast the stability accurately for the safety of the grid. Weather it is in terms of Gradient Boosting Tree Algorithm or any other traditional algorithm, these machine learning models are successful in achieving the objectives of the task but they lack a forthcoming metric to assist in high stake situations, uncertainty quantification. The paper is devoted to the analysis of the reliability of smart grid systems based on Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN) taking into account both the reliability of predictive modeling and forecasting uncertainty. The smart grid stability augmented dataset was used to benchmark the efficacy of using BNNs or BNNs combined hybrid models, one with XGBoost, for feature extraction and the other with LightGBM. The present study shows that the BNN used with the above mentioned smart grid system achieved an accuracy of 92% with precision of 0.89, recall of 0.91 and F1 of 0.90. These metrics are appending with the help of the additional features of BNN where they are capable of addressing the key questions around uncertainty and thus the metrics confirming the predictions are quite strong in terms of real-time grid stability evaluation. This article encapsulates a detailed study of BNN architecture, the role of uncertainty in machine learning models and the natural application of such models in the design of dependable and fault-tolerant smart grids.

articleTitle: Hybrid PCA-Based Machine Learning Models for Predictive Analytics in Urban Health Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid PCA-based approach is proposed for predicting the respiratory imbalance in an urban health monitoring system. To do this, three models namely Random Forest, XGBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) were integrated into one system to improve the probability of prediction while maintaining the trade-off with the dimension reduction - a common variable in big data tasks (which, this effort is focused on). Several variables regarding the environment and health of the patients were used to form a dataset that was later transformed with the help of PCA meaning the results would get better because models with better dimensionality tend to perform better. The Hybrid PCA + MLP model produced the best accuracy which 99% and AUC - ROC which 0.90, there were also 99% produced by XGBoost but AUC - ROC was 0.83. Random forest produced “slightly” less accurate predictions of 95% with an AUC - ROC of 0.72 however; this proved the best method in terms of the computational burden since the training time recorded was about 0.55 seconds, which was lower than that of XGBoost 0.45 seconds and MLP 0.94 seconds. These findings show that hybrid PCA based models do not only improve the accuracy of predictions made but also reduce the amount of computational resources needed, which is ideal for tasks that occur in real time whereby smart urban health monitoring is a part of a bigger CPS system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Event Detection in Unbalance Active Distribution System Using Reinforcement Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: With integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) in the distribution system (DS), the power quality has decreased causing large deviation in voltage, frequency and, especially during disturbances, the security of the system may lose due to the maloperation of the relays. However, effective event detection can reduce the outage time and initiate faster restoration of the healthy section. Furthermore, the data collected from the DS is large in volume and variety and hence, to capture the accurate information from those data during any disturbance, is difficult and demands application machine learning techniques for event identification. In this paper, a Q-learning algorithm, is proposed for accurate event detection in distribution system following a disturbance. The previous and subsequent events data is utilized to identify the event. On the basis of events, the corresponding actions include isolating faulty sections, facilitating fast restoration, and load reduction as necessary. The efficacy of these algorithms is evaluated through simulations conducted on the IEEE 33-bus system with integration of photo-voltaic, utilizing MATLAB/SIMULINK 2023 and Jupyter Notebook and necessary actions are derived following the disturbance. The results obtained are satisfactory.

articleTitle: Advanced Testing Strategies to Ensure Integrity and Reliability of Earthing System in EHV Substations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Earthing systems are fundamental to the safety, reliability, and operational stability of Extra High Voltage (EHV) substations, providing effective fault current dissipation and personnel protection. This paper investigates the critical role of earthing systems, emphasizing the maintenance, testing, and performance of earth grids, particularly in aging substations. The study highlights the consequences of improper earthing, including elevated safety risks and operational inefficiencies, and provides recommendations for optimal testing frequencies to ensure system health. Additionally, innovative methods for reducing earth grid resistance in both existing and new substations are explored, along with strategies to mitigate challenges posed by environmental factors and infrastructure aging. By addressing these aspects, the paper offers practical insights for engineers to design, maintain, and enhance earthing systems, ultimately improving the safety and performance of EHV substations.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on MPPT Methods for Enhanced Photovoltaic System Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In renewable energy research, maximizing energy conversion in solar photovoltaic systems under changing climatic circumstances is a major problem. Photovoltaic systems' optimum point of maximum power extraction is complicated by variable irradiance, temperature, and partial shadowing. Multiple Maximum Power Point Tracking methods have been developed to handle this issue, each having pros and cons. This review study evaluates the latest MPPT methods for uniform and non-uniform irradiance situations, with an emphasis on partial shade. MPPT approaches are classed as classic, soft computing, and hybrid. Performance under diverse shading circumstances, algorithm complexity, and tracking speed. Hybrid approaches, which blend traditional and intelligent algorithms, may improve tracking efficiency but are more complicated to apply. This document helps researchers and engineers choose the best MPPT technique for their solar system applications based on efficiency and cost.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Energy Storage Systems for Maximizing Renewable Integration in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: To address climatic change and reduce carbon emissions, the usage of non-conventional resources like solar and wind, are rapidly increasing every day. Depend on the irregularity of the nature, there are some challenges in Electrical grids, for maintaining supply consistency and balancing the grid stability. To overcome the challenges, power storage systems (PSS) play an important role due to the preserve extra energy generated during their peak time of low demand and deliver it when the power supply demand is high. This capability maintains grid flexibility by providing a reliable energy supply. Recent advancements in PSS technologies, including battery storage systems, flywheel batteries, supercapacitors, hydrogen storage, and hybrid energy storage systems (HESS), aim to improve essential Qualities like energy capacity, efficiency, scalability, and cost-effectiveness, making these systems more available for extensive implementation. The AI and ML applications used for present energy management allow flexibility in power grid operations. Additionally, hydrogen storage combined with fuel cells is emerging as a promising long-term solution. To manage seasonal variations energy backup systems, play a crucial role by preserving extra energy during the time of peak generation and delivering it when the power generation is less in renewable energy. Moreover, an innovative approach for energy optimization in the smart grids by integrating electric vehicles (EVs) used as mobile energy buffers and to enhance overall grid flexibility, when non-conventional power production is less. EVs will store energy and supply it back to the network during peak time and two-way operating through the power from grid to vehicle. This review highlights the essential roles, of ESS and EVs in smoothing the development of low-carbon, sustainable energy systems, particularly smart grids designed to maximize renewable energy combinations while assuring grid stability.

articleTitle: Protection Coordination Study and Recommendations for a Real Time Operational Wind Farm with Type-1 and Type-4 Wind Turbine Generators
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Renewable Energy (RE) is the clean and green energy and it has undergone fast expansions worldwide especially in the last two decades. Wind power generation is gaining popularity across the globe and it poses lot of challenges as well like intermittency in nature, power grid integration, inertia, stability, security, protection issues and transient stability. Comprehensive protection schemes are compulsory to improve network system reliability, transient stability of the network and to ensure Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) connectivity to the grid under different fault conditions. In this paper, the existing real-time operational wind farm is modelled and simulated in Electrical Transient and Analysis Program (ETAP) software. IEC 60909 standard is followed for load flow calculations and short circuit analysis. Existing Protection schemes are evaluated and relay coordination is undertaken for both Type 1 and Type 4 WTGs. Relay coordination is carried out using Normal Inverse Definite Minimum Time Lag (IDMTL) characteristics for 22 kV feeders, power transformer LV side, HV side and 110 kV Grid side, as per IEC 60255-151:2009 which is the latest standards. Also, a suitable optimal relay setting is recommended for proper sequence of operation and to maintain reliability of the power system networks.

articleTitle: A Novel Meta-Heuristic Algorithm Based $\text{PI}(1+\text{PI})$ Controller for Automatic Generation of Power System Integrated with Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The affordability and long-term sustainability of renewable energy have garnered significant attention in recent times. The large-scale integration of a photovoltaic (PV) system into an existing power infrastructure is a difficult task. It is difficult to regulate frequency because of the inconsistent irradiance and inertia-less system. Thus for multi-area power systems with PV and thermal plant sources, load frequency control is proposed in this article. In a two-area hybrid power system that combines a PV system and a reheat thermal system, the aim of this research is to investigate how the AGC operates. A PI(1 + PI) controller is implemented in order to enhance system performance. To fine-tune controller parameters, GCRA, a recently developed optimization technique is adopted. In AGC processes, this method has never been investigated before. The integral of time-multiplied absolute error (ITAE) objective function is used in the optimization process. This article provides a comparative analysis between firefly algorithm (FA), salp swarm algorithm (SSA), genetic algorithm (GA) and shuffled frog leaping algorithm (SFLA) which are well-known methodologies found in the literature and the performance of the GCRA based PI(1+PI) controller is analyzed under various scenarios. According to comparison analysis, the proposed controller performs better than cutting-edge methods in terms of undershoot and overshoot values for changes in tie-line power as well as system frequency variations. This research offers important insights into how well the GCRA tuned PI(1+PI) controller manages AGC operations in intricate hybrid power systems.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Approach for Protection Coordination in a Microgrid Using JADE Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: A protection strategy utilizing agent technology for adaptive relaying of Directional Overcurrent Relays (DOCRs) has been proposed in this paper. In this approach, communication plays a vital role by providing real time information of the changing system conditions. In this study, communication channel has been simulated in Java Agent Development Framework (JADE) platform. The change in topology has an adverse impact on the protection coordination of the DOCRs and hence, the settings of DOCRs should be updated. In this study, for 9-bus test system communication channel flow has been established between different agents of the system, namely, relay agents, DG agents, equipment agents etc through Agent Communication Language (ACL) standard. Different test cases have been considered, namely, DG connection/disconnection, line outage, change in microgrid operation and relay coordination upon occurrence of fault for enhancing the protection strategy. In this study communication channel between different agents has been carried out through series of simulation on JADE platform for different contingencies in the quest to validate the sequence of events that occur upon fault inception. Hence, the DOCRs adaptively update their settings utilizing the communication channel and mitigate any maloperation of the relay. This ensures greater reliability and efficiency in mitigating the relay coordination problem.

articleTitle: Bad Data Detection Using Residual Measurement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: As technology is rapidly advancing across the globe, also the power demand is simultaneously increasing, creating a pressing need for sustainable and reliable energy sources. Conventional energy sources are no longer sufficient to meet this demand, prompting the exploration of non-conventional energy sources such as wind and solar power. This has led to the transformation of traditional grid systems into more dynamic, interconnected cyber-physical power systems (CPPS), where physical systems, communication networks, and control systems work in synergy. Smart grid systems, with their reliance on sensors, meters, and communication networks, are vulnerable to cyber-attacks, making cybersecurity a critical area of research. This paper proposes a method for detecting bad data in cyber-physical power systems using residue measurement. The approach is tested on a standard IEEE bus system, highlighting that even minor data discrepancies can significantly impact system performance. The identification of bad data (IBD) is a challenging task, particularly within tight time constraints. The residue measurement technique offers a reliable, state estimation-based solution for identifying bad data in near real-time, making it a valuable tool in ensuring the integrity and security of smart grids.

articleTitle: Enhancing Economic Power Delivery: A Squirrel Search Algorithm Approach Addressing Realistic Power System Constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: On complex economic dispatch (ED) issues with valve position impact, restricted practicable region, ramp borders, and manifold fuels with valve position impact, the effectiveness of the Squirrel Search Algorithm (SQSA) approach has been demonstrated. The simulation results obtained with the suggested method are comparable to those obtained with other acknowledged evolutionary methods. Based on the comparison, it appears that the advocated SQSA strategy may yield a more satisfactory response.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach of TabNet and Transformer-XGBoost for Predicting Traffic Flow in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: A smart city's transportation system can be en-hanced if there is an accurate prediction of the traffic flow which develops in an area as time goes on. This article investigates the relative accuracy of predicting traffic flow at target intersections in a city, taking advantage of two models: Tab Net and a hybrid Transformer-XGBoost. Several metrics including Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Coefficient of determination (R2 score) among others were employed to evaluate the models employed. A sequential deep learning model known as Tab Net triumphing in the competition with MSE, RMSE, and MAE being 34.48, 5.87, and 3.73 respectively, and R2 score as high as 0.917, although performing well while enhancing identification of features such as year and junction. On the other hand, while reporting similar R2 score as low as 0.184, the Transformer-XGBoost hybrid model had structuring limitations where complex interdependencies and time variations were involved recording MSE, RMSE and MAE as 338.52, 18.40 and 13.24 respectively. The graphs of residuals and QQ plots served to uncover that the hybrid model failed making a right prediction during high traffic volume days, as general tabnet results shown in the final graphs are more stable. Following investigation of the models in this study, the researchers suggest implementing TabNet as a better option for traffic management explaining its high accuracy and providing valuable guidance for cities. This would result in improvement of the traffic flow prediction, which is highly needed for effective urban mobility solutions.

articleTitle: A Zeta Converter-Based Improved BLDC Motor-Driven Water Pumping System for Partial Shading Environment of Solar PV
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a brushless DC motor (BLDCM) fed water pumping system driven by the solar photovoltaic array (SPVA) under dynamic partial shading conditions. For extraction of maximum power from SPVA, a zeta converter (ZC) is utilized. However, under partial shading conditions, the SPVA experience multiple maximum power points (MPP). The conventional MPP tracking methods are ineffective in identifying the global MPP points as they converge to the local MPP points. Therefore, the utmost power cannot be extracted, when SPVA working under partially shaded conditions. Thus, this paper demonstrates the use of hybrid perturb & observe and particle swarm optimization techniques to track the global MPP. In this work, the SPVA's power extracted by ZC is fed to BLDCM for water pumping application using VSI. The VSI of a BLDCM typically functions at a significantly high frequency. This work proposes operating the VSI at a fundamental switching frequency to alleviate difficulties associated with high switching frequency. The suggested system is studied in MATLAB®/Simulink environment to validate its performance under various operational instances.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Short Duration Power Quality Disturbances Using Short Time Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The present power system have been charac-terized by high dynamics due to advances such as the accessorial loads, switching power supply equipment and enhancement of power system regulations. The power quality (PQ) analysis was earlier performed using Fourier Transform (FT) where parameters such as time-amplitude variations and frequency-amplitude variations were used. However, these parameters focus on the stationary power quality disturbances(PQDs) and cannot capture non-stationary or short duration PQ disturbances. Modern power systems need a broader viewpoint based on the amplitude, duration, and frequency of interruptions. In this paper, Short Time Fourier Transform(STFT) is proposed for identification of short duration PQDs which include voltage sags, swells, interruptions, transient oscillations and harmonic. In this paper, power quality disturbances will be assessed by Short-Time Fourier Transform which enhances PQ analysis under dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Slime Mould Algorithm –Based Study on Optimal Placement Planning of Capacitors and Distributed Generations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The increasing load demands in distribution systems are giving rise to several issues, including higher line losses due to increased current flow and deterioration of the system voltage profile. To address these challenges, this study employs and validates a method for the optimal placement and sizing of Distributed Generations (DGs) and Capacitor Banks (CBs) on a standard 118-bus distribution system. An unconventional objective function is utilized, incorporating system line losses, cumulative voltage deviation, reliability index, and overall system cost, to obtain the optimal solution for the problem. Initially, a sensitivity analysis, based on power loss and cumulative voltage deviation indices, is performed to identify the most appropriate bus locations for deploying DGs and CBs. Thereafter, the maiden application of slime mould algorithm is made to address the aforementioned problems. The independent and simultaneous optimal deployment of DGs and CBs are studied as separate case studies, and their results are compared and analyzed to highlight the relative advantages of each approach.

articleTitle: Role of Grid Forming Converters in Microgrid Clusters for Load Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Maintaining frequency stability across multiple micro-grid clusters presents a significant challenge. This study introduces a benchmark dynamic model of an isolated microgrid cluster interconnected via tie lines, incorporating various types of distributed energy resources. This paper investigates a multitude of energy storage systems to primarily maintain the balance between supply and demand of power and also to maintain the target grid frequency at the scheduled value. The relatively low inertia characteristic of hybrid power systems results in substantial frequency fluctuations in response to minor load changes within microgrid clusters. This phenomenon underscores the critical need for robust and efficient and grid forming converter technologies, which are discussed in this paper. The developed model is employed to analyze the frequency behavior of networked microgrids highlighting the role that power electronics converter technologies can offer in microgrids. The effectiveness of the study is demonstrated using time domain simulations performed in Matlab<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textregistered$</tex> environment, revealing improvements in frequency and tie-power deviations with more than 60 % overshoot reduction, substantiating overall system performance.

articleTitle: Optimized Cluster Head Selection and Routing in WBANS Using Hybrid Improved Particle Swarm and Adaptive Cuckoo Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBASN) or Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBAN) have gained significant importance in medical applications and are now crucial for patient monitoring. Among other processes, routing is still considered a resource-intensive activity. Hence, it is imperative to develop a routing system for WBAN that optimizes energy use. Current routing algorithms prioritize energy savings over security. Nevertheless, security assaults result in heightened power consumption and diminish the overall network performance. WBAN, among others, employs node clustering as a strategy to address this problem. In order to accomplish the desired selection of CH (Cluster Head) for IoT devices, we take into account optimization aspects such as distance, latency, and power consumption. This work presents a sophisticated approach for selecting and routing CH (cluster head) using a combination of hybrid improved particle swarm optimization (IPSO) and adaptive cuckoo search optimization (ACSO). Using the ACS algorithm, the study applies energy-efficient opportunistic routing to control the network lifespan. This approach removes the data aggregation delay of the smart wearable patch and effectively prevents routing loops. Next, we evaluate the system's efficiency in terms of network lifetime, latency, error indicators, energy efficiency, and network performance. We carry out this study effort using the MATLAB software. We perform the simulations under diverse circumstances. In terms of energy use and network longevity, the suggested method is better than the most recent cutting-edge methods, such as Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH), PSO, Ant Lion Optimization (ALO), and hybrid IPSO-ACSO.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning Approach for Differentiating Simultaneous Temperature and Strain Impacts on Apodized FBG-based Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) is incorporated with proposed functional profile of apodization to illustrate the significance of average range of side lobes scale moderation in the spectral response by apodization approach for effectively determining the target measurands. The Bragg wavelength alters based on the impact of measurands that might affect the periodicity in addition to the amplitude of modulation index of the FBG. To determine the responses of the specific measurands effectively, it is exceedingly worthwhile to figure out whether the modifications in the Bragg wavelength are attributed through the responses of temperature or strain, as both target measurands influence the Bragg wavelength alteration. The utmost challenging aspect of implementing FBG is the cross-sensitivity issue amongst the temperature along with the strain responses on FBG. Several Machine Learning (ML) approaches are incorporated through Ensemble Learning based models (like-Extra Trees, Random Forest, Bagging, and AdaBoost) to resolve the drawback of cross-sensitivity of FBG sensors through multi-out regression analysis of target measurands. The predictive analysis performance of the Ensemble models with AdaBoost regressor for the differentiation of the temperature together with the strain influences is noted as significantly high as compared with the other models.

articleTitle: Review and Comparison of DC-DC Buck Boost and Boost Converter Topologies for Fuel Cell Integration in Electric Vehicles and Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Fuel cells are gaining widespread attention for their eco-friendly energy generation capabilities. To seamlessly integrate fuel cells into applications like electric vehicles and microgrids, it's crucial to employ power converters that align the bus voltages to the voltages of FC voltage. Various DC-DC buck-boost and boost converters, each with unique pros and cons, are extensively discussed in recent research. This paper endeavours to gather, contrast, and elucidate different DC-DC buck-boost and boost converter designs introduced in recent studies, aiding in informed decision-making for efficient fuel cell integration.

articleTitle: Advanced Wind Power Forecasting Using Parallel Convolutional Networks and Attention-Driven CNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for the effective integration of wind energy into power grids. Yet, the inherent variability of wind and the intricate interplay of meteorological factors make prediction a challenging task. This study introduces a novel short-term wind power forecasting method, improving the traditional convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) model through two significant innovations. First, we introduce a parallel convolutional architecture that employs both 1dimensional (1D) and 2-dimensional (2D) convolutions to simultaneously capture temporal patterns and inter-variable relationships in wind power data. This structure, inspired by Explainable-CNNs, enables more comprehensive feature extraction. Second, we integrate an attention mechanism that dynamically weights the importance of different input features and time steps, improving both forecast accuracy and model interpretability. The proposed model is evaluated using data from two wind farms in Croatia, comparing its performance against benchmark models including standard CNN-LSTM, LSTM, and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks. Results demonstrate that our enhanced CNN-LSTM model achieves superior forecasting accuracy, with improvements in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 15% and 12% respectively, compared to the best-performing benchmark. Furthermore, the attention mechanism provides valuable insights into the relative importance of different features over time, offering a new level of interpretability in wind power forecasting models. This work contributes to the advancement of accurate and explainable wind power prediction, supporting more efficient renewable energy integration and grid management.

articleTitle: Advanced Distribution System State Estimation Techniques: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This study provides an outline of Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE), a technique introduced by Fred Schweppes in 1970. Since then, SE has been crucial in managing and controlling electric transmission operations. It has also played a role in enhancing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems (SCADA) as well as Energy Management Systems (EMS). DSSE has certain difficulties like high R/X ratios, unbalanced phases, inadequate current and voltage measurements, scalability problems, etc. To improve the DSSE accuracy phasor measurement units are used. study on state estimation techniques based on Branch-Current and Node-Voltages are being conducted. The methods applied for dynamic state estimation play a significant role in power systems for monitoring, control, and stability assessment. These methods are used in state estimation in power systems to enhance the system's reliability, stability, monitoring, and control in modern distribution systems.

articleTitle: An Iterative Technique for Enhancing Profitability and Dispatchability of Wind-Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: In response to the intermittent power generated by the Wind Energy System (WES) and the Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) acting as a supplementary source in parallel with WES, the work proposes to determine the optimal size of BESS in kWh. The study uses wind speed data from the WES in Gujarat, India, to determine the forecasting errors. A realistic energy cycle generation targeting forecasting errors is developed using the Normal Distribution Curve. The optimum size in kWh of BESS for supplying the deficit forecasting power is determined, and it is found that the size is not enough to recover the investment cost even in a lifetime by selling the discharged power from the BESS at the Day Ahead Market (DAM) prices of Indian Energy Exchange at each time block. The study then investigates the profitable option through BESS by feeding power to the grid more than the forecasting error at favorable DAM prices and determine the kWh size of the BESS. An iterative technique is proposed for the maximum profitable discharged power. In the investigation process, an upgrade technique is also proposed to upgrade the initial size of the BESS in case of State of Charge (SoC) limit violations. The results are compared with the Genetic Algorithms (GAs) to justify the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Novel Hybrid Algorithm for Investigation of Dissolved Gas Analysis for Alternate Dielectric Fluids of Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The power transformer is the most important element of equipment in an electrical transmission and distribution network. The power and voltage levels that these transformers can manage determine their size, and as the transformer's volume increases, internal isolation and cooling become more challenging. The most popular insulating fluid used in transformers for insulation and cooling is mineral-based oil, which has demonstrated exceptional dielectric and thermal qualities. However, alternative oil technologies have been sought to replace mineral-based oils in recent years because to concerns about safety, cost, and environmental impact. In this context, extensive research efforts have emerged on biological oils for use in transformers. This paper examines the sustainability, safety, and electrical performance of bio-based ester oil in transformer applications with respect to dissolved gas analysis (DGA). AI-based Fuzzy logic controller (FLC) with Duval's triangle (DT) and Duval's pentagon (DP), IEC, CIGRE reports are used in a hybrid manner to identify the possible incipient faults inside the oil-immersed transformers. The graphical analysis of various fuzzy logic plots along with DT and DP are utilized to critically analyze the possible incipient faults arrayed due to DGA. The proposed work proficient compared to previously published results. Highest efficiency of DT and DP based FLC (92%), followed by furan analysis (82.3%). Lastly, recommendations are made on potential fixes for the problems raised and the future course of study for alternate dielectric fluids-based power transformers. The suggested techniques in this research offer a higher diagnostic accuracy than the present approach.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review of Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities and Safety Concerns in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) are among the leading technologies enhancing our world with their advanced autonomous driving capabilities and functional awareness. These AVs rely on sophisticated technologies such as weight sensors, speed sensors, tire pressure sensors, 3D imaging cameras, satellite-based positioning systems, and advanced radars like light detection and ranging (LiDAR) and 3D radar. AVs utilize these components, along with highly complex control algorithms as their central processing units, to perform autonomous driving, making them vulnerable to cybersecurity attacks. These security attacks raise significant safety concerns for AVs. This article provides a comprehensive review of various cybersecurity threats associated with AVs and presents potential solutions. Additionally, it examines the vulnerabilities of the sophisticated equipment used in AVs. This article aims to enhance the understanding of the safety and security concerns associated with AVs and offers insights into the importance of cybersecurity in this evolving technological field. Furthermore, this article addresses the current state of cybersecurity measures in AVs, evaluating the effectiveness of existing protocols and identifying areas that require improvement. It also explores emerging technologies and strategies that can enhance the security of AVs, such as blockchain for secure data transactions, machine learning for threat detection, and robust encryption methods.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Power Loss Analysis in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This research estimates the power loss in photovoltaic (PV) systems through a Random Forest model by using 15-min interval data for two years (2021–2023) of operation from a university campus located in Delhi, India. Irradiance, temperature and the dust concentration were used in the analysis to calculate and estimate actual and theoretical potentials and power losses based on factual, modelled and theoretical determinations under Standard test conditions (STC). Seasonal changes are of particular interest and therefore, the power loss is to be analyzed based on three power quality reports obtained over three different seasons in 2023. The results of the model show the Mean absolute error (MAE) to be 29.145 W along with Root mean square error (RMSE) to be 57.72 W. Interactions with power loss observed seasonally proved to have variations in dust and power loss, temperature, and so on; all of which confirmed the effectiveness of Random Forest model in providing valuable predictions of season-sensitive data. These results would be significant to enhance the efficiency of the PV system and how energy technologies for dusty areas should be designed.

articleTitle: Hybrid PV and Battery-Powered Inverter for BLDC Speed Control with Hall Effect Feedback
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents an optimized control strategy for a Brushless DC (BLDC) motor driven by a photovoltaic (PV) system, incorporating Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) using the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method, Field-Oriented Control (FOC), and battery storage. The Proportional-Integral (PI) controller for motor speed regulation is optimized using the Bat Algorithm (BA), improving performance metrics such as settling time, steady-state error, rise time, and overshoot. Hall Effect sensors provide accurate rotor position and speed feedback, enabling precise commutation and control. The MPPT algorithm ensures maximum power extraction from the PV panel under varying sunlight conditions, while a DC-DC boost converter increases the voltage. to the necessary level for the BLDC motor. The battery storage system ensures continuous operation during periods of low solar input. Simulation results indicate that this design effectively harnesses solar energy, providing stable motor operation under changing load and irradiance conditions. It is well-suited for applications such as electric vehicles, water pumping systems, and robotics, offering a sustainable off-grid power solution for BLDC motor-driven systems.

articleTitle: Planning and Analysis of Possible Land Utilization Patterns for Food-Energy Park With Renewables
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: With the growing demand for clean energy and sustainable agriculture calls for proper land use and developing smart infrastructure to increase both food and energy yield. In this regard, food-energy park (FEP) concepts are emerging as a good option for achieving food and energy security. This paper presents a detailed plan for land utilization and techno-economic analysis of a prototype FEP on a one-hectare (2.5 acres) plot, integrating renewable energy generation with sustainable food production. The FEP aims to meet a renewable energy capacity of 500 kW and produce enough food for 50 people. A comparative analysis of separate zones for different renewable energy sources (RESs) and farming with respect to combined or mixed zone that installs RESs side by side with plantation rows. The study covers the planning and pre-installation analysis of each zone, modeling of the land use area, problem formulation with application of predictive algorithms, and conducting a comprehensive techno-economic studies. The results highlight the feasibility of the FEP, offering insights into the balance between energy production, food yield, cost efficiency, and environmental impact.

articleTitle: Renewable Power Integration for Electric Vehicle Charging System: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This review paper accentuates on the conceivable integration of renewable based generations to the charging stations of Electric Vehicles (EVs) towards restraining the carbon emissions. The intensifying global demand for EVs in recent days puts stress on conventional grid with existing infrastructure, which could be relaxed by integration of renewable based power generations with ecological balance. The importance and feasibility of renewable integrations to charge the EVs are reviewed in this paper and suitable applications are reported to develop charging infrastructures for EVs. The importance of vehicle to grid (V2G) concept is also reviewed to facilitate ancillary support to future grid integrated with renewables.

articleTitle: Core Power Control of a Pressurized Water Reactor Using Event Triggered PID Control
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper introduces the implementation of an Event-Triggered (ET) Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-tuned Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller for regulating core power in a Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR). It addresses load-following challenges in PWRs by ensuring precise and rapid tracking of demand power while optimizing resource usage. Traditional time-triggered PID controllers continuously compute control signals, resulting in high computational loads. In contrast, the ET based PID control law reduces resource consumption by minimizing unnecessary control updates while maintaining accurate power tracking. The controller activates only when specific events occur, significantly reducing computational effort and control signal communication. Additionally, by limiting redundant control actions, the system's controllers and actuators experience less wear and extended operational life. The PWR state-space model incorporates key parameters such as coolant temperature coefficients, control rod reactivity, and thermal power, enabling dynamic adjustments to control rod positions and speeds in response to power demands and system conditions. Simulation results confirm that the proposed ET based PSO-tuned PID controller effectively addresses the load-following issue in PWRs. The findings indicate enhanced performance, reduced computational burden, and stable reactor power within operational limits under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Forecasting the Impact of High Solar Module Temperature on Power Output and CO2 Mitigation: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The effects of high solar module temperatures on photovoltaic (PV) systems in power output and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> mitigation were explored. The researchers made the predictions of temperature oscillation impacts on PV system performance and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions reductions using Linear Regression and Extra Trees Regression models. Results of the research work using Linear Regression gave a higher R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value in power output prediction, namely, 0.9992, while Extra Trees Regression provided an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.9993 for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions mitigation. Data pre-processing techniques involving imputation, outlier detection, and feature engineering techniques were applied to ensure proper data quality. The empirical study finds that temperature influences both PV system performance as well as the potential reductions in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Machine learning models outperform conventional techniques by providing more dynamic analysis based on data and better precision. These findings emphasize the role of temperature management in the optimization of energy efficiency of PV systems and reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, hence furthering the effectiveness of solar energy systems in climate change mitigation.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation Using Advanced Fractional Order-Based Controller in Interconnected Power Systems Involving EV Aggregator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: As the global population grows, so does the demand for power. When demand exceeds generation, system frequency decreases, leading to instability. Both single-area and multi-area power systems face frequency stability issues. Load frequency regulation is key to maintaining reliable power delivery. In this work, a fractional order proportional tilt integral derivative (FOPTID) is developed for the load frequency control issue for a two-area interconnected multi-source power system. The efficacy of the FOPTID controller is compared with the traditional controllers like PID and FOPID by adapting it to the two area system. The designed system is then tuned using a recent optimization, i.e., sea horse optimization (SHO), for optimally deriving the optimal controller parameters. The vehicle model (EV) is incorporated in area-2 so that the frequency profile can be enhanced. Finally, it is observed that the SHO-tuned FOPTID controller performs better and produces optimal responses. The proposed FOPTID with the electric vehicle model results in minor transients in frequency and tie-line responses and settling of frequency to the desired 50Hz at a quicker time.

Author Keywords: fractional order proportional tilt integral derivative (FOPTID) controller

articleTitle: Portable Battery Bank for Emergency Power During Natural Disasters: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Energy scarcity is increasing exponentially, due to the rise in population and modernization, to overcome the problem we need to find an alternate solution. This study explores repurposing retired electric bus batteries as compact charging stations within a solar nano-grid system, offering offgrid emergency power. The technical and economic viability, emphasizing battery and solar panel performance. The retired battery contains nearly 80% of its capacity and remains intact, making it suitable for energy storage. The proposal extends battery life, targeting a second-use scenario, lasting 6 to 30 years based on usage. The waste of EV batteries is hazardous to the environment and organisms and can be overcome by reusing them in disaster. The combination of off-grid power and solar panels enhances efficiency, reliability, and emergency response. This concept is economical, thereafter making it a viable approach for remote regions and disaster relief. This approach showcases retired batteries as assets for sustainable off-grid energy through solar integration. The studied system is modelled in MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Daily EV Load Prediction Using Fuzzy Inference: A Microgrid Planning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The rapid rise in electric vehicle (EV) adoption highlights the critical need for a reliable charging infrastructure to ensure the stability of power distribution networks. This research introduces a fuzzy inference system (FIS) designed to forecast daily EV loads essential for developing microgrids to meet the increasing demand for EVs. The present work considers four factors for FIS designing: travel distance, parking duration, battery state of charge (SoC), and expected arrival times at charging stations. By developing fuzzy logic rules for these variables, a probabilistic charging is generated, improving both the precision and adaptability of load forecasts. This study also explores the impact of future EV adoption on microgrid load demand, analyzing adoption rates of 53%, 68%, and 84%, providing crucial insights for planning microgrids. The discrepancy between estimated and actual EV loads is found to be 0.078, demonstrating a reduction in prediction error. This effectively mitigates uncertainties related to EV user behavior and supports the design of resilient and flexible microgrid systems.

articleTitle: Mitigating Low Inertia Challenges in Renewable Energy-Based Microgrids: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) into power systems has significantly reduced system inertia, increasing frequency deviations and the Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF). This paper examines the challenges associated with low-inertia power grids and investigates solutions to maintain stability in systems dominated by renewables, with a focus on advancements from 2020 to 2024. Accurate measurement technologies and advanced computational methods are critical in addressing these issues. Key research areas include Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESS) and Gravity Hydro Storage (GHS), both of which are extensively studied for their potential to deliver rapid inertia response and stabilize frequencies during disturbances. Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) and Synchronous Condensers have received moderate attention, offering practical but less innovative solutions. Emerging technologies such as Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) Synchronization, Batteries, Ultra-capacitors, and Self-Synchronized PLL are underexplored yet hold immense potential for future research and development. Hybrid inertia solutions are highlighted as a critical pathway for ensuring reliable grid performance. These systems combine the strengths of various technologies to provide both short-term frequency stabilization and long-term energy support. Additionally, the study emphasizes the importance of precise inertia estimation tools and advanced control algorithms to address the unique challenges posed by large-scale RES integration. A comprehensive and forward-thinking approach is essential to manage the transition toward renewable energy dominance. This includes leveraging cutting-edge technologies and fostering innovation in underexplored areas to ensure the stability and resilience of modern power systems.

articleTitle: Signal Processing and Soft Computing Techniques Driven Analysis of Chhattisgarhi Dialects Using MFCCs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Chhattisgarhi, spoken by over 12 million people in Chhattisgarh, is the most prominent, holding official language status and serving as a cultural and linguistic identifier. Baheliya and Chamari, though less documented, are vital to the region's linguistic diversity. This research investigates the acoustic and phonetic characteristics of three central Indian dialects—Chhattisgarhi, Baheliya, and Chamari—using advanced machine learning techniques and robust feature extraction methods. Leveraging Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) for feature extraction, this study examines statistical parameters such as mean, median, and variance to distinguish the spectral properties of these dialects. Our contribution includes a detailed analysis of dialectal variations, revealing that Chamari exhibits the highest mean MFCC1 value (0.223), indicative of its higher spectral energy, while Chhattisgarhi shows the most negative mean MFCC2 (-0.322), reflecting unique spectral distinctions. Variance analysis highlights Baheliya and Chhattisgarhi as having greater spectral diversity, particularly in MFCC1 and MFCC2, showcasing their phonetic variability. These findings underline the acoustic uniqueness of each dialect, bridging gaps in existing research on underrepresented dialects. This work contributes to the preservation of linguistic diversity and provides a strong foundation for designing ASR systems tailored to regional dialects, addressing critical challenges in multilingual speech recognition.

articleTitle: Generation of PWM for 2-level Inverter on Modern Microcontrollers: A Generic Algorithm Leveraging on Waveform Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The inherent symmetries and periodicity of signals based on sinusoidal functions are leveraged to develop a computationally efficient firmware algorithm for generating pulse width modulation (PWM) gating signals on a modern microcontroller for voltage source inverters (VSIs). This method involves creating PWM directly through firmware by utilizing scalar carrier comparison methods for various PWM schemes, including Sinusoidal PWM (SPWM), Third Harmonic Injection PWM (THIPWM), Space Vector PWM (SVPWM), and Discontinuous PWM (DPWM). By exploiting the symmetry and cyclic nature of reference signals, the novel approach allows for the reuse of calculations across different phases under steady-state conditions. Synchronizing the carrier wave period with the symmetries of the modulation reference signal further allows the use of quarter-wave symmetry to simplify pulse width calculations and reduce memory requirements. The algorithm also incorporates pipeline and pre-calculations of certain parameters to efficiently determine embedded timer counter values. Additionally, the firmware, written in ‘C’, supports dynamic switching between different modulation schemes. Practical results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness with a 3-phase 2-level VSI controlled by an ARM Cortex M4-based microcontroller equipped with a CORDIC trigonometric math unit.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Based Optimization of Hybrid Solar PV, Hydrogen, and Battery Storage Systems to Maximize Energy Production
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and sustainable energy resources has emphasized the need for hybrid energy systems.
