The integration of intermittent solar PV systems and battery storage systems presents a significant challenge in achieving controlled and maximized energy production. This study optimizes energy production in a DC microgrid system, integrating solar PV, a electrolyzer, and a controllable battery storage subsystem. Additionally, it proposes a Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework that enhances coordination control of the storage system and operational efficiency within the microgrid. By allowing discrete agents as a PV availability, to make decisions and interact with the energy storage system, the framework adapts dynamically to changes in energy demand and available supply, maximizing energy and hydrogen production. The results demonstrate that the multi-agent approach achieves higher energy output compared to conventional optimization techniques, like Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MIP), using yearly PV datasets in Indian scenarios. This study is performed using the Python PuLP tool, and the simulation findings include improved battery storage utilization and real-time energy dispatch. The proposed approach contributes to the development of MARL based solutions for hybrid energy systems, with implications for enhancing sustainability in distributed microgrids.

articleTitle: Controlling and Performance Evaluation of DC Microgrid Using Adaptive Control Integrated with Blue Whale Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a new method for regulating and assessing DC microgrid performance: adaptive control combined with the Blue Whale Optimization (BWO) algorithm. Improving DC microgrid efficiency, stability, and dependability under a range of load and generation scenarios is the goal. The adaptive control technique responds to microgrid variations by dynamically adjusting control settings in real-time. These control settings are optimized using the BWO algorithm, which is based on the foraging behavior of blue whales and guarantees optimal system performance. Numerous simulations were run in order to evaluate the suggested system's efficacy. Comparing the results to conventional control approaches, it is clear that there have been significant gains in voltage regulation, power quality, and overall system efficiency. Adaptive control combined with BWO significantly reduces disturbances and increases the microgrid's resistance to errors and variations. This methodology exhibits exceptional flexibility and resilience in handling the varied and sporadic characteristics of sustainable energy resources inside the microgrid. By providing a bio-inspired optimization strategy, the findings expand DC microgrid control methodologies. This work highlights the possibility of using evolutionary algorithms in conjunction with adaptive control to attain the best possible operational performance in contemporary energy systems. The suggested approach paves the way for further study on intelligent control strategies in smart grid applications while also improving the operational reliability of DC microgrids.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Various Classifiers in Detecting Incipient Fault Type Using DGA Data
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) is a popular technique for incipient fault detection of power transformers. Machine learning (ML) algorithms are reported to be efficient in incipient fault detection using DGA data. Selection of input features and data balancing plays a crucial role in determining the fault classification accuracy of various ML classifiers. In the present work, Density-Based Clustering is first used to obtain a Euclidean distance feature using the gas concentration values of DGA data. The present work compares the performance of popular ML classifiers using input features constituted by gas concentration, gas ratios and the Euclidean distances of the fault points using DGA data. Various performance indicators are calculated to compare the performance of the tested ML classifiers.

articleTitle: Indigenous Design and Development of Interface Board for TMS320F28335 DSP and Programming via MATLAB Simulink Embedded Coder
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: This paper presents an indigenous design and development of an interface board, interfacing different micro-controller peripherals and sensors, for the Texas Instruments TMS320F28335 Digital Signal Processor (DSP), with a focus on its integration with MATLAB Simulink Embedded Coder to do efficient programming and code deployment. The developed interface board, having essential hardware, provides a reliable and seamless connection between the TMS320F28335 DSP and the development environment, enabling real-time control, signal and data processing tasks for various embedded control systems. MATLAB Simulink Embedded Coder is employed to generate C code for the TMS320F28335 through automatic code generation and direct deployment of algorithms to the DSP streamlining the development process for embedded applications. This paper discusses the hardware components of the interface board along with communication protocols and configuration of various C2000 microcontroller blocks for software integration with MATLAB, highlighting its versatility and ease of use for real-time embedded system development. A case study of real-time implementation of closed-loop v/f control of induction motor is presented and the obtained results demonstrate the efficacy of the interface board while enabling its efficient programming and operation. This work contributes a viable, customizable solution for the students, researchers, and engineers started working with TMS320F28335 DSPs and Embedded Coder, promoting enhanced productivity and flexibility in embedded system development.

articleTitle: Multi-Area Economic/Emission Dispatch with Arctic Puffin Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Multi-area economic emission dispatch (MAEED) deals with the determination of the optimum generation schedule of each power generating unit and power transfer between connected areas at minimum cost and minimum emission both while satisfying all associated operational constraints. In this paper first formulation of the complex MAEED problem has been carried out, and then it is implemented to solve using Artic Puffin Optimization (APO). APO is inspired by ecological processes i.e. survival and predation behaviour of the arctic puffin. The efficacy of APO has been investigated on two standard test cases of four area MAEED problems. They are 16 and 40 power-generating unit systems. The obtained results by simulation show that APO is very promising for solving complex highly constrained optimization problems.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Microgrid Energy Management Using Renewables and Storage Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: The inherent variability and unpredictability associated with solar and wind energy resources can be adeptly addressed and managed through the comprehensive integration of various power generation systems that exist within hybrid energy microgrids, ultimately ensuring the provision of a reliable, stable, and economically viable energy supply for consumers and industries alike. The potent amalgamation of varied renewable energy realms, in conjunction with state-of-the-art energy retention apparatus, into intricate energy oversight frameworks holds an essential position in profoundly amplifying both the longevity and efficacy of electricity generation mechanisms, as well as the utilization trends of electric power across a multitude of applications and domains. A wide array of innovative energy management algorithms and control strategies is thoroughly investigated and analyzed, highlighting the continuous and pressing need for ongoing advancements and improvements aimed at optimizing the utilization of renewable energy sources alongside the latest storage technologies, all to substantially enhance the total performance and reliability of energy systems in various contexts. The control of microgrids fundamentally revolves around the effective and efficient management of distributed generators (DGs), which necessitates an intricate understanding of their operation and the implementation of advanced control mechanisms to ensure optimal performance and integration within the larger energy network.

articleTitle: Design and Development of DC Inductor for Hybrid Circuit Breaker Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: With the advances in semiconductor technology like wide band gap-based power electronics, there is an increased focus on hybrid circuit breakers (HCBs) instead of the traditional mechanical circuit breakers to improve the response time to fault currents. These HCBs play a critical role in protection of electrical systems like DC microgrids. However, HCBs suffer from reliability and life reduction if exposed to very high rates of current rise during the initial transients. This paper proposes a DC inductor placed in series with the HCBto reduce the rate of current rise. In this work electromagnetic simulations have been performed on various inductor designs to finalize the type of core, its height and the number of copper winding turns based on performance metrics like inductance and limiting current. The finalized inductor design has also been analyzed using coupled electromagnetic-thermal analysis (finite element analysis) to ensure that the design meets temperature limits for all the materials. The inductor design has been prototyped and tested to validate the results of thermal simulations.

articleTitle: Inertia Estimation Through Local Frequency Measurements and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Increasing penetration of non-conventional energy sources into traditional power systems introduces variability in system inertia over time. Converter-dominated power grids exhibit dynamic behaviors that significantly differ from those of traditional synchronous systems, rendering existing power system models inadequate for precise inertia estimation. In this paper, a Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)-based methodology is proposed for inertia estimation, utilizing local frequency measurements to provide an adaptive and robust solution. A pulse excitation signal is applied to induce system perturbations, with frequency deviations captured through a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL). The proposed CNN model demonstrated an accuracy of 94.35%, with estimated inertia values deviating by less than 10% from actual measurements and achieving a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.3865. When validated on previously unseen frequency data, the model maintained a comparable performance, yielding an RMSE of 0.3996. This data-driven, model-free approach presents a substantial advancement over conventional inertia estimation techniques, particularly in addressing complexities introduced by renewable energy sources and their impact on system dynamics.

articleTitle: The Role of Hydrogen Fuel Cells in Evolving Electric Vehicle Market
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 1st International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Developments in Electrical Engineering (SSDEE)
abstract: Nowadays the automotive industry is moving towards sustainable transportation solutions. To achieve this Hydrogen Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (HFCEVs) and Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs) are two well-known substitutes to traditional Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles. This paper focuses on individual EV types along with Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats (SWOTs) and their importance. Also presents the evolution of Hydrogen Fuel Cells (HFCs) in EV applications and the environmental impacts and infrastructure accessibility. The analysis of performance metrics, cost, and prospects emphasizing innovation and government policies is elaborated. This paper also confers the impact of hydrogen engines and the transition from hydrogen engine vehicles to HFCEVs. Finally, a case study on Toyota Mirai is presented to highlight the significance of HFCEV.
